scenarios.draft: Test the ability to search for admin users based on their active state and a specified grant date window. First, create multiple admin records with different grant and revocation dates. Then, use this endpoint to filter only currently active admins (where revoked_at is null) and whose grant timestamps fall within the chosen period. Verify that only admins matching the search criteria are returned and that the results are paginated correctly. This validates both temporal and state-based filtering logic for privilege audits and admin lifecycle reviews.

dependencies.purpose: Create several admin records with distinct grant and revocation timestamps to establish test data for filtered search scenarios.

scenarios.draft: Verify that searching by partial user_identifier returns all admins whose identifier includes the search fragment, supporting use cases like quick lookup or SSO-based admin audit. Set up test data with several admins whose user_identifier values have predictable overlaps. Perform a PATCH search using part of a known identifier and confirm that all, and only, matching records are returned. Also, check that pagination and ordering work as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create several admin records with overlapping user_identifier fragments to test the partial match search ability.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a single admin's details by their unique UUID. Create an admin and then use their id to fetch the record. Confirm that the returned object matches the creation attributes, including user_identifier, grant and revoked timestamps. This verifies correctness of retrieval and data integrity for privilege and compliance audit workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Create the admin whose id will be used to test single record retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Validate the response behavior when attempting to fetch an admin with a non-existent UUID. Use a random or deleted adminId and confirm that a 404 or error object is returned, without leaking data about any other admin. This tests error handling and information disclosure control for privileged entities.

Verify that an administrator can retrieve the complete details of a specific audit log record using a valid auditLogId. First, create a valid audit log entry using the admin creation endpoint and capture the generated ID. Use this ID to request the details, and confirm all relevant fields (actor, action, timestamps, etc.) are returned. The test asserts correct functioning and completeness of the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid audit log record to obtain a valid auditLogId for retrieval testing. This must be done as an admin to ensure proper audit trail creation.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that requesting an audit log record with a nonexistent or random UUID as auditLogId returns a 404 error or a descriptive not-found response. This test validates error handling for invalid references and proper security, confirming no sensitive data is leaked for missing or unauthorized records.

As an administrator, attempt to create a new audit log record providing valid actor, target, action_type, and action_detail fields as per schema. Verify that the system returns the created record with system-generated ID and timestamps, and confirm all provided and default fields are present and correctly persisted.

Attempt to create an audit log as admin while omitting one or more required fields (e.g., action_type or actor). Check that the system rejects the request and returns a validation error, ensuring that business rules require all mandatory audit details.

Test that an existing audit log entry can be updated successfully by an admin. First, create an audit log entry, then use its auditLogId to update specified fields (such as action_detail or target). Verify that the update is reflected in the returned object, and all fields (including system-managed ones) remain consistent. Changes should be properly persisted and traceable for audit purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create an audit log record to acquire a valid auditLogId for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a non-existent audit log entry using an invalid or random auditLogId as admin. Validate that the API returns a not-found error response and does not alter any data. This error scenario checks robust error handling for invalid update targets.

Attempt to update an audit log record while authenticated as a user without admin privileges. Confirm that the system refuses access and returns an authorization error, proving enforcement of role-based restrictions on audit log modification.

dependencies.purpose: Create an audit log record with admin privileges to obtain a test auditLogId for update.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a valid admin can delete an existing audit log entry by auditLogId. First, create a log entry and retrieve its ID. Then, issue a delete request and confirm the record is removed (returns 204 or similar). Follow up by attempting to fetch the deleted record and ensure a not-found error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new audit log entry to obtain a valid auditLogId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete an audit log using a nonexistent auditLogId. Confirm that the endpoint returns a not-found error and no data is erroneously deleted.
Attempt to perform a delete operation on an audit log without admin rights. Ensure the system responds with an authorization error, verifying access control enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create an audit log entry to supply an auditLogId for the deletion attempt while not logged in as admin.

scenarios.draft: As an admin, retrieve the paginated list of system notices. Confirm that the response includes all system and category-level notices, regardless of active status or scheduling (active, inactive, and future notices). The test should confirm visibility of inactive and pending notices only for admin role, validating business logic on scope of returned notices for administrators.

dependencies.purpose: Create several system notices with varying is_active values and scheduling (some active, some inactive, some scheduled for the future) to ensure results include all cases.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that when there are no system notices present in the database, the endpoint returns an empty list with correct pagination metadata (no errors, empty array). Useful for verifying behavior on a clean or newly initialized system.

Test listing system notices with various pagination and filtering options, such as page size, page number, and filters (e.g., by category, active status). Ensure that the correct subset of records is returned, pagination works as intended, and edge cases (such as partial last pages) are handled properly.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple system notices across categories, with different statuses, to test filtering and pagination features.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can successfully retrieve the full list of all discussion board moderators. Verify that the response includes each moderator's user identifier, grant date, and revoke date where present. The list should contain currently active and previously revoked moderators as per schema. If no moderators exist, an empty array should be returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one moderator record to ensure the returned list is not empty during testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that non-admin users (e.g., regular members) are denied access or receive a forbidden error when attempting to fetch the list of all moderators. This validates proper security enforcement on sensitive role data access.

Test the ability to filter moderators using an advanced search query specifying a user_identifier substring. Verify that only results matching the query are returned and pagination works as intended. Test includes both active and revoked moderators.

dependencies.purpose: Insert multiple moderator records with varying user identifiers for search coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for moderators using grant and revoked date ranges. Provide test data for both currently active moderators and previously revoked ones. Verify that only moderators matching the specified state and date criteria are returned in the paginated result.

dependencies.purpose: Create moderator records with differing grant and revoke states for advanced filtering.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that submitting a malformed or logically invalid search query (such as an unsupported field or invalid date format) results in a user-friendly error response and does not return moderator data. Test error handling for robust admin tools.

Test retrieval of moderator details by a valid moderatorId. The response should accurately reflect all persisted fields from the moderator record, including user_identifier and audit timestamps. Confirm data integrity and that all fields match what was submitted during creation or update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator to obtain a valid moderatorId for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to retrieve a moderator by a non-existent or random UUID returns a not found (404) error response. Ensures the system does not leak details of existing users or moderators, and that error handling is robust.
Test that non-admin users (such as regular members) cannot access details of moderators by ID and receive an appropriate forbidden error. Validates strict role-based access control.

Test creation of a new discussion board moderator with proper user_identifier and grant timestamp. After creation, validate that the returned record contains the correct fields, is persisted in future GET requests, and grant/revoke status is accurate. Also verify business rule: user_identifier must be unique; attempt duplicate creation in separate scenario.

Attempt to create a moderator with a user_identifier that already exists in an active moderator record. System should reject the request and return a duplicate/uniqueness constraint violation error. Ensures integrity of moderator assignments.

dependencies.purpose: Create initial moderator with a unique user_identifier before attempting the duplicate.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a moderator record with missing required fields (e.g., omit user_identifier or grant timestamp). System should return a detailed validation error, and no moderator record should be created.

Test updating an existing moderator record by setting the revoked_at timestamp, effectively revoking privileges. Verify that subsequent GET requests reflect the updated status and that revoked moderators no longer appear as active. Confirm audit trails are accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator whose privileges will be revoked in the update test.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a moderator's user_identifier (e.g., after SSO/email change) and verify the persisted data is accurate. Ensure update is blocked if the new user_identifier collides with an existing record (covered separately). Confirm changes are audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator to be updated with a new user_identifier for this test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a moderator record using a non-existent UUID. System should return a not found (404) error with no side-effects.
Test that only admin users can update moderator records. Attempts by unauthorized users should result in a forbidden error. Ensures privileged operations are protected.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a moderator record for attempted unauthorized update by a non-admin.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new discussion board setting with a unique key, valid value, and optional description by an authorized admin. Admin should be able to create the setting when all data is valid. Validate that the returned object includes the new id, timestamps, and values. Ensure audit log is updated. Dependencies: Admin user must be logged in and have permissions.

Test creating a new discussion board setting where the setting_key already exists. Admin attempts to create a setting with a duplicate key and expects an error indicating uniqueness violation. Validate that the existing settings are not affected and proper error response is returned to the client. Dependencies: The initial setting with the key must already exist, created by the admin.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial setting with a unique key, so that a duplicate key scenario can be tested.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a setting using a reserved or special system key that requires extra validation. The system should return an error or warning if the key is restricted according to business policy. Audit logging should record the attempt even if rejected. Dependencies: Admin authentication.

Test updating an existing discussion board setting with valid changes (such as new value or description). Ensure the update works, the returned object reflects changes, timestamps are refreshed, and audit log is written. Dependencies: There must exist a setting to update, and admin must be authenticated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a settings row to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a setting to use a key that already exists on another settings row. The system should return a uniqueness/validation error, and no changes should be made. Audit logs should note the failed attempt. Dependencies: At least two distinct settings must already exist before the update attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first setting with key A.
Create the second setting with key B; the test will attempt to change B's key to A.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a setting using a non-existent or malformed settingId. The system should return a not found or validation error and not alter any records. Audit systems should log the failure. Dependencies: Admin user authentication.

Test deleting an existing discussion board setting by its ID using admin privileges. The setting must be successfully removed from the system (hard delete), and subsequent retrieval should fail. Audit logs should capture the deletion for compliance. Dependencies: A setting must exist in the database prior to deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a setting that will be deleted in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a setting with a non-existent or already-deleted settingId. The system should return a not found error, and the operation should be properly logged for compliance. Dependencies: Admin authentication (no specific data setup required).

Test that an authenticated admin can retrieve a paginated list of all audit logs. Ensure that logs include key metadata (actor, action, timestamp) with correct ordering. Validate that no audit logs are omitted and pagination behaves as expected. Dependencies: Audit logs must exist, so the system should have prior actions such as settings creation or deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Perform actions that generate audit logs for listing, such as creating settings.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving audit logs when no records exist in the database. The response should be an empty list and the system must not error. Useful at initial platform setup or after test data has been cleared. Dependencies: No pre-existing audit logs required.

Test advanced search functionality for audit logs by applying filters like actor, action_type, or date range. The response must only include matching records, correctly paginated and filtered. Dependencies: The system must have multiple distinct audit log records created by different actors and actions.

dependencies.purpose: Trigger at least two distinct actions that result in different audit logs to enable meaningful filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test searching audit logs with invalid or unsupported query syntax (e.g., invalid date range or unrecognized filter key). The system should return a validation error and not process the request. No records should be returned. Dependencies: Admin authentication; no specific data setup needed.

Test advanced search of activity logs by a moderator using role-type and specific date range filters. A moderator requests activity logs filtered by actor_role (e.g., member, moderator) and within a specific time interval for audit or investigation purposes. The scenario should confirm correct filtering, pagination, and error handling for invalid filters. It should also verify that results only include permitted log data, and access is denied for unauthorized users. Validation is required for malformed filters or attempts by non-privileged roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create baseline activities as audit log entries to ensure there is available data to search/filter upon.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific activity log entry using its unique activityLogId. The scenario should include preparing at least one known log entry, retrieving it using the correct ID, and verifying that all attributes returned match the created entry. It must confirm that access is granted only to admin or authorized roles and that non-existent activityLogId returns a not found error. The result should also show how missing privileges are handled.

dependencies.purpose: Insert a new log entry to have a known and retrievable activityLogId in the system for testing retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator retrieval of a specific activity log entry by unique activityLogId. A moderator attempts to fetch the log for detailed audit review. The scenario should validate that the correct data and all log fields are returned for valid requests, and that access is denied for roles lacking sufficient privileges. Also test the response when a non-existent log ID is requested, ensuring a clear error is returned. Compare success for moderator role to failure for non-moderator attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create a known log entry so the activityLogId exists for detail retrieval and access validation.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully create a new activity log entry recording an event, ensuring all mandatory fields (e.g., actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, timestamp) are validated and stored. Include validation of business constraints and schema rules. Also test error handling for missing required fields, invalid references (e.g., non-existent actor or target), or unauthorized attempts. Check that logs are properly saved for later audit, and audit logging is triggered upon creation.

Ensure that a moderator can create a valid activity log and that the system rejects creation attempts by unauthorized or unprivileged users. Cover both successful creation with valid data and failure scenarios, such as missing required fields, actor_id referencing a non-existent user, or attempts to spoof actor_type. Audit trails should reflect the correct creation event and actor info. Include a scenario where a guest or member tries to create an activity log and is rejected for permission.

Test that an administrator can successfully delete a moderator assignment by providing a valid moderatorId. First, create a member and assign them as a moderator. Then, as an admin, attempt to delete the moderator using their moderatorId and expect a 204 No Content response. After deletion, attempts to fetch the removed moderator should result in a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will then be promoted to moderator for setup.
Assign the created member as a moderator to generate a valid moderatorId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the failure scenario when an admin tries to delete a moderator assignment using a moderatorId that does not exist. Expect a 404 Not Found or relevant error response indicating the moderator assignment does not exist.

Test that non-admin users (such as members or moderators themselves) are forbidden from deleting moderator assignments. Attempt the delete operation as a non-admin and expect an authorization or permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a non-admin member to simulate an unauthorized delete attempt.
Create a moderator assignment to attempt deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve a complete list of all board members. The result should include all members ever registered in the system, each with their ID, user_identifier, join timestamp, and suspension status. Verify that members created in setup appear in this list with accurate details.

dependencies.purpose: Create several member records to populate the members table before listing.

scenarios.draft: Test that access to the list of members is forbidden for non-admin users. Attempt to retrieve the list with a user lacking the admin role and verify an authorization or access denied error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member to simulate permission denial scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that the admin can perform advanced search/filter with criteria such as finding suspended members, searching by user_identifier, and applying pagination. Ensure search results match filters and respect pagination settings.

dependencies.purpose: Create members with a mixture of suspended and active statuses and various user_identifier values for filter coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test that using an invalid filter (e.g., malformed query or search by a non-existent field) yields a user-friendly error and does not crash the API.
Test that performing search on members is restricted for non-admin users. Attempt to use the endpoint as a non-admin and verify a permission denied error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member for the unauthorized search attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test the retrieval of a member's full details by memberId as an admin. Confirm the returned data includes all expected fields, and the memberId corresponds to a real user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member in order to retrieve their details using the generated memberId.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when requesting member details with an invalid or non-existent memberId. Expect a 404 Not Found or meaningful error response.
Test that non-admin users are forbidden from retrieving a member's details. Attempt to access the endpoint as a member and expect an authorization error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to use for the unauthorized detail access.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new board member using valid user_identifier and join timestamp. Verify the member record is created and persisted with all required attributes.

Test that creating a member with a duplicate user_identifier is rejected according to unique constraints. First, create a member, then attempt to create another with the same user_identifier and expect an error indicating duplication.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial member with a unique user_identifier to test duplication.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when required member creation fields (such as user_identifier or join timestamp) are missing. The API should return a validation error identifying the missing fields.
Test that only admins can create new members. Attempt member creation as a non-admin and expect a permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular (non-admin) user to use in permission test.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that a board member can successfully update their own comment's content. Precondition: a member and a comment owned by them must exist. Attempt to update the comment's content with non-empty, valid new text. Expect successful update and returned comment reflects the changes.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new board member to serve as the comment author.
Create an initial comment associated with the member to provide a commentId for updating.

scenarios.draft: Check that updating a comment by a member who is not the original author is denied. Prepare two member accounts: A (author) and B (unauthorized). Member A creates a comment; Member B attempts to update it. Expect an error indicating lack of permission. Validate no changes to the original comment.

dependencies.purpose: Register two board members: A and B.
Member A creates an initial comment; its commentId is updated by unauthorized member B.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to update a comment with invalid data (such as empty or excessively long content) fails validation. Use a member's own comment as target. Try updating with empty string or content exceeding system length limits. Expect validation error and preservation of original comment.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for the comment author.
Create a comment to be updated with invalid data by its owner.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that updates are not permitted on comments that have been soft-deleted (is_deleted flag set). Have a member create and then soft-delete their comment, then attempt to update it. Expect failure with appropriate error and no update applied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as comment author.
Author creates a comment.
Comment owner soft-deletes (is_deleted=true) their own comment to set up the scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test admin's ability to permanently delete any comment. Scenario: Admin logs in, retrieves a comment (created by any member), and deletes it using the correct commentId. Expect the comment to be removed, and subsequent lookup returns not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will author a comment.
Have the member create a comment to provide a valid commentId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Verify that deleting a comment that does not exist (random or already-deleted commentId) results in a not-found error. Admin attempts to delete a non-existent comment and expects a 404 error response.

Ensure deletion is prevented when performed without admin privileges. Attempt to delete a comment as a non-admin (e.g. regular member or moderator), expect a permission-denied error and no deletion occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular board member and have them author a comment.
Member creates a comment to provide a commentId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully perform a permanent deletion of any comment. Scenario: Moderator is authenticated, identifies an existing comment with a valid commentId, and performs the delete operation. The comment is removed, and subsequent queries return not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member to author a comment.
Member creates a comment to serve as the target for moderator deletion.

scenarios.draft: Check that deleting a non-existent comment as a moderator correctly returns a 404 error. Use a random or already-deleted commentId and ensure no accidental data manipulation occurs.
Confirm that comment deletion is not allowed if performed by a user without moderator or admin rights. Attempt a hard delete as a regular member, expect a permission-denied or equivalent error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member and have them author a comment to be used in the test.
Create a comment using the non-privileged member's account.

scenarios.draft: Ensure the comment author can retrieve version history for their own comment. Create a member, have them create a comment, perform edits to produce versions, then request the version list as the author. Response should list all historical versions, including timestamps and editor information.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member.
Member creates original comment.
Member edits (updates) their comment multiple times to create additional versions.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a user who is neither the author nor an admin/moderator cannot access another member's comment version history. Scenario: Member A creates and edits a comment. Member B requests version list for A's comment and is denied access.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members: one as author (A) and one as an unauthorized accessor (B).
Member A creates a comment and edits it for multiple versions.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully retrieve all edit versions for any comment on the board, even if not the author. A member creates and edits a comment; a moderator requests its full edit/version history. Ensure full visibility of all versions and editor metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member (comment author).
Create and edit (multiple versions) a comment as the member to provide test data.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for topics with advanced filters: by category and pinned status. First, ensure there is at least one category and a pinned topic in that category. Use the PATCH /discussionBoard/topics endpoint to search for topics belonging to that category and with the pinned flag set to true. Verify that the response only includes pinned topics in the specified category. Additionally, test with a non-existent category and confirm no topics are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Retrieve a list of categories to use a valid categoryId as a search filter.
Create a topic in the chosen category and set the pinned flag to true to ensure data exists matching the filter.

scenarios.draft: Test the search endpoint by using a combination of filters (such as title, category, and date range) that do not match any topics in the system. Expect an empty result array and proper pagination metadata, confirming the system handles 'no results' states gracefully and does not throw an error.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a valid categoryId to use as a filter for which there are no topics.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search with invalid data types or malformed filters (e.g., non-UUID values for category, non-boolean for pinned, or unsupported fields). Validate that the system returns a clear validation error and does not process the search.

Create multiple topics in a single category and then use the PATCH /discussionBoard/topics endpoint with pagination parameters (such as limit and offset) to ensure that results are paginated correctly. Verify page size limits, total count, and navigation through all pages to confirm correct pagination behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Retrieve an existing categoryId to create multiple topics in.
Create more topics in the target category than the standard page size to test pagination.

scenarios.draft: Validate the ability to retrieve detailed information of an existing topic by its topicId using GET /discussionBoard/topics/{topicId}. Expect the returned object to match the topic created (title, description, category, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic to obtain a valid topicId to fetch.

scenarios.draft: Try to fetch details for a topicId that does not exist in the system. The API should return a 404 not found or a specific error response indicating the topic is missing.
Request topic details with an invalid UUID format as the topicId (e.g., by passing a non-UUID value). Confirm that the API returns a validation error and does not accidentally leak data.

Test creating a new topic with all valid fields (title, description, category, and flags). Validate success response and that the returned object contains all provided and auto-generated data. Confirm by fetching or listing topics in that category.

dependencies.purpose: Retrieve an active categoryId to use in topic creation.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a topic with a duplicate title in the same category, which should be disallowed. First, create one topic, then attempt to create another with the same title in the same category. Expect a conflict or validation error for title uniqueness.

dependencies.purpose: Retrieve a valid categoryId and ensure it exists.
Create the first topic with a unique title to test for duplicates.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a topic in a category marked as inactive. The API should reject the creation and return an appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: Find or identify a category that is inactive for use in the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a topic without some required fields, such as missing title or categoryId. Validate that the API returns clear validation errors for each missing field.
Ensure that a user with moderator privileges can successfully create a topic. All valid fields should be accepted, and the response verified for correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Collect a valid/active categoryId to associate with the new topic.

scenarios.draft: Test that topic creation as a moderator without the required title field fails with proper validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Category selection for test context is required.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to have a moderator create a topic in an inactive category, which should be rejected, confirming that even moderators cannot create topics in inactive categories.

dependencies.purpose: Identify an inactive category for testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create two topics with the same title in the same category as a moderator. The second attempt should be rejected as a uniqueness violation.

dependencies.purpose: Get a valid/active category ID for topic creation.
Create the initial topic to set up the duplicate title scenario.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can create a new topic with all required and optional fields set, receiving a success response and the correct persisted data. Cross-check the result by retrieving the topic to confirm all values are stored.

dependencies.purpose: Fetch a valid, active categoryId for associating the topic.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when an admin attempts to create a topic without providing a categoryId field. Should receive a validation error indicating the missing category.
Attempt to create a topic as an admin in an inactive category. The API is expected to reject this action according to business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Identify an inactive category for testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin cannot create two topics with the same title within the same category. The second creation attempt should be rejected with a clear uniqueness violation error.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a categoryId for the scenario.
Create the first topic to trigger duplicate title logic.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of a moderator to search for moderation actions using advanced filters, such as filtering by action type, moderation date range, target entity, and actor. First, ensure that at least a few moderation actions exist in the system by creating sample actions through standard moderator workflows (such as resolving a report or flag). Then, attempt to search moderation actions with different criteria and verify correct filtering and sorting. Success criteria include paginated, accurate results according to provided filters, and proper authorization enforcement (non-moderators should not get access). Edge cases include requesting out-of-range pages and using invalid filter syntax.

dependencies.purpose: Create a few moderation actions to ensure there are records to filter and paginate in the search. These actions will be used as the data set for the search tests.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can execute complex search/filter queries on the moderation actions table. Begin by ensuring the existence of a diverse set of moderation actions representing different actors, target entities, and action types. Use the search endpoint with combinations of filters for actor type, action type, period (date range), and target entity. Validate that the results honor all applied filters, correct sorting options, and pagination. Test for robustness against malformed search conditions and ensure that only admin (and moderator) roles can access. Edge cases include searches with zero matches and oversize page requests.

dependencies.purpose: Create several moderation action records from the admin role to provide data for subsequent search and filter operations.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve complete details for a specific moderation action by its unique ID. First, create a moderation action via typical moderator workflow. Fetch its ID and attempt to retrieve it using this endpoint. Verify the returned record accurately reflects the stored metadata and that all related fields (actor, target, action details) are populated. Confirm that error handling works for non-existent IDs and invalid formats. Authorization must restrict access to moderators/admins only.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderation action as a prerequisite, so that there is a valid moderationActionId available for the GET detail test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can access all details of a given moderation action by providing its unique identifier. Set up by creating a moderation action as an admin, record the returned ID, and then retrieve it using this endpoint. Check that all fields are present and accurate, including actor and target references. Include tests for not found (invalid ID) and forbidden access when using insufficient privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderation action as an admin to ensure there is a valid moderationActionId for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully create a new moderation action by providing all required data. Start by ensuring required foreign keys (such as a valid report, post or comment to reference and an existing moderator account) are available. Attempt to create an action with valid input and confirm the returned object reflects the new state. Test failures include missing or invalid references (such as referencing a non-existent target), missing required fields, or invalid enum values. Ensure that audit logs capture the creation event and that unauthorized attempts (such as from a non-moderator user) are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new report that may serve as the reference target for moderation action test data.
Create or ensure existence of a moderator account for actor association on the moderation action.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a discussion board category by an admin when there are no dependent records (such as topics or moderator assignments). First, create an admin user, then create a new category with no topics or assignments. Attempt to delete the created category and verify that the operation completes successfully and the category is no longer present in listing endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user who will perform category creation and deletion.
Create a new category as an admin to ensure it can be deleted and is not referenced by other records.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to hard-delete a discussion board category that is referenced by dependent records (e.g., there are topics in this category). Create an admin, create a category, then create a topic within that category. Attempt to delete the category and verify that an error is returned indicating deletion is blocked due to dependencies.

dependencies.purpose: Establish an admin user for all admin-only actions.

Test that non-admin users (e.g., members or moderators) cannot delete reports. Attempt to delete a report as a moderator or member and verify permission is denied and the report is not removed.

scenarios.draft: Test listing moderation actions using various filtering parameters (such as action type, creator, or target type) as a moderator. Confirm paginated results match filter criteria and are returned in the expected order. Cover scenarios with zero results and large result sets.

scenarios.draft: Test listing moderation actions as a user without moderator or admin privileges (e.g., guest or member). Attempt to invoke the endpoint and verify that permission is denied and no moderation actions are returned.

Test that an admin can successfully list all moderation actions, including filtering and pagination over a large dataset. Verify result structure includes all expected moderation action attributes and no data is missing for admin users.

scenarios.draft: Test that when there are no moderation actions present in the system, an admin receives an empty result set. Confirm that pagination metadata reflects zero available actions and the response is well-formed.

Test successful creation of a moderation action record by an authorized moderator or admin. First, set up prerequisite entities: a moderator/admin account, a report or flagged content, and a valid actor/target. Provide all required fields in the request (e.g., actor, action detail, target, evidence) and verify that a moderation action record is persisted with accurate timestamps and references.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator record who will perform the action.
Create a report or flagged content that the moderation action will address.

scenarios.draft: Test that the API returns validation errors when attempting to create a moderation action with missing required fields such as actor, action_type, or missing critical references (e.g., missing target entity). Confirm that no action is recorded and an appropriate error message is returned.

scenarios.draft: Test that the API forbids moderation action creation by an unauthorized user (e.g., ordinary member or guest). Attempt to create a moderation action without admin/moderator privileges, and verify that access is denied and no action is stored.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a moderation action by a moderator. First, ensure a moderation action exists and the acting user has moderator role. Update editable fields (e.g., notes, action details) and confirm the changes are saved and properly reflected in the response.

Ensure the updater has moderator rights.

scenarios.draft: Test that updating a moderation action with a non-existent or invalid moderationActionId results in a not-found or error response. Confirm that no record is changed, and the API responds with a clear error.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action as a user lacking moderator/admin rights. Confirm that the request is denied and the moderation action remains unchanged.

scenarios.draft: Verify the system returns a not-found error when an admin attempts to update a moderation action using a UUID that does not exist. Ensure that no change is made and an appropriate error is returned.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action as a user without admin privileges and verify that access is denied. Confirm that only admins and moderators can update moderation actions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action for testing.
Create a regular member user to test permission enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin is able to permanently delete a moderation action. First, create a moderation action, then perform the DELETE operation as admin and confirm the action is removed from the system, and the deletion event is logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to later delete.
Create an admin user authorized to delete.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation action with a non-existent or already-deleted ID, and confirm that the API returns a not-found error and that no deletion occurs.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation action as a user without admin rights. Verify that the API returns a permission-denied error and that the moderation action is not deleted.

Create a member-level user to test permission enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully retrieve a paginated list of all content flags. Ensure there are some flagged items in the system and confirm the response includes proper pagination, details, and only permitted flag metadata. Verify access control enforces moderator/admin roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create content flags to be listed in the retrieval.
Ensure a moderator account exists for API access.

scenarios.draft: Verify that non-moderator roles, such as regular members or guests, cannot retrieve the list of content flags and the API returns a permission error.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where the content flag table is empty. The API should return a paginated empty result set with appropriate metadata and not an error. This verifies handling of empty state UX.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account to perform the test.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving all version histories for a specific comment as an admin. First, create a member and a new comment under a post, then perform multiple edits to create several versions (edits) of the comment. As an admin, fetch the full version history using this endpoint and verify all snapshots, editors, and timestamps are correctly listed and ordered chronologically. Confirm an empty array is returned if no versions exist, and that access is denied for non-authorized users (e.g., a random guest or unprivileged member).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new board member to serve as the comment author.

Edit the comment multiple times (as member or admin) to create several history versions.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability of a member to filter, search, and paginate the version history of their own comment. After creating and editing a comment multiple times, use the PATCH endpoint to filter by editor, date, and content keywords. Ensure the correct set of versions are returned according to specified criteria, and paginated as expected. Also, test that members cannot filter version histories of comments they do not own (expect an authorization error).

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member to generate a commentId.
Edit the comment multiple times to produce versions.

After creating a comment and producing multiple edit versions (by different editors, including member and moderator), search for all edits made by the moderator only, and validate results. Ensure results respect allowed filters and access controls, and that an error is returned if an invalid comment ID is provided.

scenarios.draft: As an admin, perform filtered and paginated retrieval of a comment's version history. Multi-edit a comment with versions attributed to both member, moderator, and admin. Use the PATCH endpoint to filter versions by time frame, editor, and content. Validate the filtering is accurate and that result paging works. Confirm that an invalid search request (e.g., out-of-range pagination) returns a user-friendly error.

dependencies.purpose: Member creates a comment to be edited by multiple actor roles.
Admin edits the comment to create admin-attributed version(s).

scenarios.draft: Ensure a member can retrieve a specific version snapshot of their own comment by versionId. After creating a comment and editing it several times, fetch a known version by its ID and verify all fields (content, editor, timestamp) match expected historic values. Test that attempting to access a non-existent versionId, or a version belonging to another member, returns an appropriate error or access denial.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment as a member.
Edit the comment multiple times and store the resulting versionIds.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully retrieve a paginated list of all content flags on the discussion board. The scenario assumes that there are flagged posts and comments on the board created through prior moderation activity. Validate that essential flag details—such as target entity, flag type, creator, and timestamps—are included and accurate, and that pagination works as expected. This test ensures the endpoint is accessible only to users with admin or moderator roles. If no flags exist, an empty result set is returned. Key validation: audit logs should reflect access attempts for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create content flags on posts or comments so the listing operation yields meaningful results.
Assign an admin user to invoke the GET endpoint with proper privileges.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that non-admin and non-moderator users (such as regular members or guests) are denied access to the content flags list, returning a 403 forbidden or a suitable unauthorized error. This test confirms permission enforcement to protect sensitive moderation data. Attempts by unauthorized actors should be logged for audit. The system must not leak any flag metadata under these conditions.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for positive control testing.
Register a regular member who will attempt unauthorized access.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator or admin can retrieve a filtered, paginated list of content flags using advanced search parameters such as flag type (e.g., spam, abuse) and creation or clearance date ranges. The scenario includes setup of multiple flags with diverse types and timestamps, then executes queries filtering for a specific type and time window. Verify the response includes only matching flag records and the pagination metadata is correct. Edge cases: filter returns no results, or limiting to a recent window.

dependencies.purpose: Create several distinct content flags of different types and timestamps for filtering.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can perform a patch (advanced search) for content flags filtering by target type (e.g., post vs comment), using pagination and sort options. The test assumes existing flags of both target types and verifies only relevant flags appear per the applied filter. The scenario demonstrates correct enforcement of advanced filtering business logic and validates role-based access control for admins.

The test sets up a new flag on a post or comment, then fetches its details, validating all returned metadata such as flag type, creator, target entity, notes, and all relevant timestamps. The scenario ensures the endpoint returns a clear error if the flag does not exist or if an unauthorized user attempts access. This workflow is critical for moderation review and decision-making.

scenarios.draft: Validate that the admin receives an appropriate error (such as 404 not found) when requesting a content flag by an ID that does not exist in the system. dependencies.purpose: Set up an admin user with permission to make the GET request.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully retrieve the details of a specific user or guest session by supplying a valid userSessionId. First, create a valid session record as a user or guest via /discussionBoard/userSessions (POST), then as an admin, fetch this session's details and confirm all relevant fields are returned as stored. This scenario proves that audit, troubleshooting, and forced-logout workflows can be performed by admins as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid user or guest session record to ensure there is a session to retrieve as an admin.

scenarios.draft: Verify the system returns an appropriate error when an admin attempts to fetch details of a user/guest session using a non-existent or invalid userSessionId. Attempt to retrieve with a made-up or previously deleted session ID as an admin, and confirm that an error response, such as 404 Not Found, is returned without leaking any sensitive information.

Attempt to fetch user session details without proper admin rights, such as using a member or guest role. The system should deny access and return a permission error to non-admin requestors, demonstrating security compliance over session data.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a session when a registered member logs in. Begin by ensuring a member account exists (registration can be done via the appropriate member onboarding endpoint if available). Then, submit a session creation request with valid actor_type 'member', a unique actor_identifier (e.g., the user's ID or handle), a secure session_token, and valid timestamps. Validate that the system responds with the persisted session details and all expected attributes, including created timestamps and status flags.

Test that a new guest session record can be created by submitting an anonymous guest visit, providing a unique actor_type 'guest', a random session_token, and required timing fields. Confirm that the session is saved and returns all required fields. This scenario ensures tracking for non-authenticated users is compliant with analytics and system requirements.

Attempt to create a session record while omitting one or more required fields (e.g., missing actor_type or session_token). The API should reject the request and return a validation error indicating which required property is missing, preventing incomplete or invalid session records from being stored.

Attempt to create a session with a session_token that is already actively associated with another session (if unique constraint exists). First, create a valid session. Then, attempt to create another session with the same session_token. Expect a conflict error indicating session token must be unique to prevent session hijack or accidental overlap.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can mark a user session as terminated by setting the terminated_at field for a valid session ID. First, create a new session (via the POST endpoint), then as an admin, update this session's record to include a valid terminated_at timestamp. The response should reflect the changes, and further validation should show the session as terminated in the system.

Attempt to update a session as a user who lacks admin privileges (e.g., as a regular member or guest). Expect a permission error to ensure session management remains restricted to system administrators for critical actions like forced logout or expiry extension.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a session with an invalid or already deleted userSessionId as an admin. The system should respond with an appropriate error (404 or equivalent), verifying robust error handling and no silent drops.

Test that a logged-in member can retrieve the same paginated list as a guest, but with validation that their authenticated status either returns the same topics or, if requirements permit, may include member-exclusive topics. Confirm correct topic visibility and access control.

Test the endpoint's behavior when there are no topics in the database (e.g., after all are deleted or in a brand-new system state). Confirm that it returns an empty result set without error and with correct pagination structure, supporting clean UI rendering for first-load or no-content scenarios.

Test the paginated listing's integrity while topics are being created or updated concurrently (e.g., simulating rapid posts in a busy board environment). Verify that pagination remains consistent and handles new additions between requests gracefully, without duplicate or missing data across page loads. This ensures stable browsing in real-world user activity conditions.

Verify that an admin user can successfully delete a content flag by specifying a valid contentFlagId. Prior to the deletion, ensure that a content flag exists by having a moderator or admin create one via the POST /discussionBoard/admin/contentFlags endpoint. Deletion must result in the content flag being removed (hard delete)—subsequent attempts to access the deleted flag should return a not found error. Audit logs should confirm the deletion action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content flag to be deleted in the scenario. Must be done first to obtain a valid contentFlagId.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a content flag using a invalid or non-existent contentFlagId as an admin. The system should return a not found error and no deletion occurs in the audit logs. This tests error handling for incorrect flag references.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content flag as an admin so a non-privileged user can attempt deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple subscriptions for various users and topics/threads to test filtering and pagination.

scenarios.draft: Submit a PATCH search on subscriptions using filter criteria that do not match any existing records (such as a non-existent subscriber or target). The response should be an empty paginated list with no error.

Ensure the API only returns the authenticated member's subscriptions even if other subscriptions exist (for other users), and that filter results are correct for created subscriptions.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a subscription for a different user to exist in the system.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a guest or logged-in user can successfully retrieve a list of all discussion board categories with default pagination settings. The response must include a flat list of categories with correct metadata for each (name, description, parent category if any, active status, timestamps). No authentication or special permissions are required. Also validate that the active/inactive statuses and parent-child relationships are accurately represented in the response. The test should cover cases where categories are both root and nested.

Ensure that when there are deeply nested categories (multiple levels of parent/child), the GET endpoint returns all categories in a flat list, but preserves the correct parent_id relationships in the response. Validate with a dataset where categories are organized with various nesting depths. Confirm the consistency of hierarchical context and the correct indication of parent-child linkage in the returned metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create root and nested categories as an admin. Root categories should be created first, followed by nested child categories referencing their parent_id.

scenarios.draft: Test the advanced filtering and search of categories by partial name match and active/inactive status. As a user (guest or member), submit a PATCH request specifying a partial name string and an is_active filter. Confirm that the filtered result contains only categories matching the given substring and activity state. This test checks server-side filtering, case insensitivity for name search, and proper pagination of the results.

dependencies.purpose: First, create multiple categories with varying names and active/inactive statuses to have a meaningful test data set.

scenarios.draft: Verify that filtering categories by a specific parent_id and created_at/updated_at date ranges returns only the relevant subset. Both guests and logged-in users should be able to access this endpoint successfully.

dependencies.purpose: Create one root category and one nested child category for use in detail lookup tests.

This verifies the system's missing resource handling, and that no sensitive information is leaked in error responses.

As an admin, attempt to create a new category providing a unique name, is_active status, optional parent_id referencing an existing category, and a description. Validate that the returned object includes all submitted details, correct parent-child linkage if parent_id is used, and that the category is correctly persisted in the system. Also check audit logging (if accessible) for the creation event. This test verifies the nominal successful flow for category addition, including hierarchical creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent category first to use as parent_id when creating a child category.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that the API rejects attempts to create a new category with a name that already exists (duplicate name constraint). dependencies.purpose: Create a category to update for the main test scenario.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a category as a user lacking the 'admin' role. The API should return a permission error and deny the update. This test covers strict authorization enforcement for schema modifications and prevents privilege escalation.
