dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member to have a valid commentId that belongs to the requesting user before attempting retrieval.

scenarios.draft: As a member, attempt to retrieve a comment created by another member that should not be accessible due to permissions or privacy settings. Validate that the API returns an appropriate forbidden or not found error per access control policy.

Attempt to retrieve a comment using a non-existent or deleted commentId as a member. Confirm that the API responds with a 404 or suitable error object, demonstrating robust error handling for missing data.

Test standard member workflow by creating a new comment under an existing discussion post. Validate that all required fields are accepted and that the response returns a complete comment record assigned to the authenticated member. Upon success, verify the comment appears in subsequent comment listing for the post.

Attempt to create a comment while omitting required fields (such as postId or content). Confirm that the endpoint responds with a clear validation error indicating which fields are missing according to schema rules.
Try to create a comment referring to a non-existent postId. Confirm that the system responds with an error indicating the post does not exist, ensuring referential integrity enforcement.
Attempt to create a comment without authenticating as a valid member. Confirm the request is forbidden or unauthorized, ensuring that only authenticated members can comment as designed.

Verify that an admin can update the content of any comment using this endpoint. The comment should reflect the modifications with updated timestamps and updated content upon successful API call. Ensure changes are audit-logged as required by moderation/audit policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment as a member to serve as the target for admin update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test the admin's ability to soft-delete a comment by setting the is_deleted property to true. Ensure that the comment remains in the database but is marked as deleted, and that this status is visible in future retrievals or listings as per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment for soft-deletion testing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a comment using an invalid or non-existent commentId as admin. Confirm that a 404 or similar error is returned, demonstrating robust error handling.

Simulate a scenario where the admin's authentication is missing, expired, or insufficient. Attempt to update a comment and verify that the API returns a forbidden or unauthorized error as required by role-based permissions.

Verify that a moderator can update the content of any comment using this endpoint, regardless of original author. Confirm that changes are reflected in the returned comment object and are audit-logged as necessary for moderation actions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to be updated by the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that the moderator can soft-delete (flag as deleted) a comment by updating is_deleted. Confirm that the status is accurately reflected in future retrievals and audit logs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment for the soft-deletion moderation test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a comment with a non-existent commentId as moderator. Confirm that a not found error is returned, indicating proper error and boundary handling.
Attempt to update a comment as a moderator when the request token/session is invalid or missing. Validate that the endpoint returns a forbidden or unauthorized error as per security requirements.

Test successful creation of a new guest session by sending a unique session_identifier and valid timestamps. Verify that the new guest object is persisted and returned, matching input values. This represents the standard site visit by an unauthenticated user. No authentication is required, but application rate limiting or abuse prevention logic should be considered out of scope for this test.

Test that creating a guest session using an existing session_identifier fails with an appropriate duplicate or conflict error, confirming enforcement of session uniqueness. This simulates accidental or malicious replay of a guest session creation. First, create an initial guest session. Then, attempt to create another with the same session_identifier and expect a meaningful error response.

dependencies.purpose: Establish an initial guest session with a specific session_identifier to create a duplicate scenario for testing uniqueness enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can update the last_seen timestamp on an existing guest session, simulating an analytics update or ongoing visit. The system should allow this update without errors and return the modified guest entity with the new timestamp. Verify that only updateable fields can be changed, and immutable fields remain untouched. Required business context: Admin privilege, guest session must exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest session first in order to obtain a valid guestId for update testing. Admin privileges are assumed for this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test the error response returned when attempting to update a guest session using a non-existent guestId. This checks system behavior for invalid or stale links and ensures appropriate not-found error handling for audit and analytics tools.

Test successful deletion of a valid guest session by guestId as an admin. This simulates admin-driven analytics cleanup or compliance-based erasure. The operation should return a confirmation (empty body or status code), and subsequent fetches of this guestId should return not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a guest session to ensure the guestId used for deletion is valid and present in the system before running this test. Admin rights required.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion attempt for a guestId that does not exist in the system. The endpoint should return a not-found error, confirming robust error handling for admin data cleanup or integrity operations.

Test successful retrieval of the complete session inventory as an admin. The response should include all session records for various actor types (admin, moderator, member, guest), reflecting the normalized session tracking schema. This scenario validates session dashboard completeness and permission enforcement. If no sessions exist, the test expects an empty result.

Test that session inventory cannot be retrieved by a user without admin privileges. Attempt to access this endpoint as a non-admin and expect to receive an authorization error or forbidden status, ensuring strict enforcement of session visibility and security controls.

Test advanced search and pagination features for session records, using filters such as actor_type (distinguishing between admin, moderator, member, and guest). The test posts complex query parameters and expects the result to match searched filters only. The operation should return results accordingly or an empty set if no matches are found. This scenario simulates session review, forced logout investigation, and compliance auditing by an authorized admin.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one guest session to ensure the search can return results when filtering for actor_type 'guest'.
Create at least one user session (e.g., for an admin or member) so that filters can differentiate by actor_type in the search results.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when an invalid or malformed search query for sessions is posted (e.g., invalid actor_type value, bad pagination params). The system should return a validation or bad request error, ensuring robust filter and query validation in session management logic.

Test an admin retrieving full details of a user's subscription using a valid subscriptionId. First, set up a board member and subscribe them to a topic or thread. As an admin, use the subscriptionId to fetch the details. Confirm all expected properties are present and match the subscription's assignment, subscriber, and notification method. This tests full admin access and role-based visibility.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new board member to act as the subscriber.
Establish a new subscription for the new member and collect its subscriptionId.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a subscription using an invalid or non-existent subscriptionId as an admin. Attempt to fetch with a random or deleted subscriptionId and verify the API returns a well-formed not found error, ensuring robust error handling for incorrect references.

Test a member retrieving details of their own subscription using a valid subscriptionId. Register a member, create a subscription for them (to a topic or thread), then as that same member retrieve the subscription. Confirm only the member's own subscription can be viewed, and all detail fields are accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new board member to test member-side access.
Create a subscription for the new member and obtain the subscriptionId.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member is forbidden from accessing subscription details belonging to another user. Register two distinct members; create a subscription for the first member. As the second member, try to retrieve the first member's subscription. The system should deny access, returning an authorization error.

dependencies.purpose: Create two separate members to test cross-access control.
Create a subscription for the first member, then attempt retrieval as the second member.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability for an admin to create a new subscription on behalf of any member. Register a member, then as admin, create a subscription to a topic or thread for the member. Confirm that the created subscription record is linked to the correct subscriber and contains all required information. This enables administration-driven engagement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new board member to receive the subscription.

scenarios.draft: Test admin attempt to create a subscription using an invalid or non-existent topic/thread ID as target. Attempt creation and verify that the operation fails with a validation or foreign-key error, ensuring invalid targets cannot be subscribed to.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will be used for subscription creation.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can successfully subscribe themselves to a topic or thread. After registering as a board member, use their credentials to create a subscription. Check that the subscription record links to themselves, uses correct delivery method, and passes all validations.

dependencies.purpose: Create/register a new member who will create their own subscription.

scenarios.draft: Test a member trying to subscribe to the same topic/thread twice. Register a member, subscribe them to a topic, then attempt a duplicate subscription to the same target. System should block or error on the duplicate per unique constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for the test.
Create an initial subscription for the member to a specific topic/thread before attempting the duplicate.

scenarios.draft: Test an admin updating the delivery method or status of an existing subscription. Set up a member and their subscription, then as admin, change fields such as notification method or active/inactive flag. Confirm the changes persist and are visible on subsequent fetch.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member to subscribe.
Create a subscription entry to be updated.

scenarios.draft: As an admin, attempt to update a subscription using a non-existent subscriptionId. Expect a not found or error response, validating system integrity and proper error reporting for update calls to invalid records.

Test successful update of existing activity log entry metadata (such as adding additional meta-data or correcting user agent/IP) by an administrator. Ensure all changes are properly recorded and that the response includes the updated log entry reflecting those changes. Audit logging of changes should also be considered as part of the business process.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log entry to update, ensuring a valid activityLogId for the test. This must be done before the update to have a modifiable record.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an activity log entry as a non-admin or non-moderator user. The update request should be denied and an error response returned, confirming that only authorized roles are permitted to modify activity logs as per security requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log entry to attempt updating, ensuring there is a record for the permission test.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an activity log entry as a moderator user, correcting fields such as user agent or IP address. The update should succeed, and the returned entry should have the new values. This scenario verifies proper moderator privileges compliance and correct update functionality.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log entry to be updated by the moderator, ensuring a valid activityLogId exists for the update operation.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update an activity log entry using an account without moderator or admin access. The operation must be denied and an appropriate permission error produced, validating role-based access control on activity log updates.

dependencies.purpose: Create a log entry as a moderator for update attempt; then use a lower-privilege account to test access control.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of an activity log by an admin. The specified log entry should be removed from the system, and subsequent attempts to fetch it should result in a not-found error. Verify that the delete operation is fully logged for compliance and that this action is irreversible due to hard delete behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log entry to be deleted for the purposes of the test, ensuring a valid activityLogId exists for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a non-existent activity log entry by specifying a random or deleted activityLogId. Verify that the system responds with a proper not-found error and that no changes occur to the audit log table.

Test authorized moderator deleting an existing activity log entry. The operation should succeed, and the record should not be retrievable after deletion. Confirm traceability by ensuring deletion is audit-logged and that only users with moderator or higher rights can perform this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an activity log entry to delete, providing a valid activityLogId for the test.

scenarios.draft: Simulate an attempt by an unauthorized user (neither moderator nor admin) to delete an activity log entry. The request should be denied and return an error indicating insufficient permissions, ensuring access control works as intended.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample activity log entry to attempt deletion with the wrong privileges.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of the paginated engagement stats list as an admin. The response should include valid engagement analytic records (such as post counts, user activity, and segment breakdowns), with all fields present according to schema. Pagination behavior should be verified by requesting additional pages if available.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more engagement stats records to ensure there is data to retrieve during the test.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch engagement statistics as a user without 'admin' privileges. The system must restrict access, returning a permission denied error and no data, thus validating proper back-office privacy enforcement.

Verify that a member can successfully update their own subscription details, such as changing notification method or activating/deactivating the subscription. First, create a board member and authenticate the session. Next, create a subscription assigned to this member via the proper API; extract the subscriptionId. Call the update endpoint as the subscription owner with a valid update payload (e.g., change delivery method). Expect the response to reflect the new values and updated metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Register a board member so a subscription can be created and updated by this user.
Create a subscription as the new member and obtain the subscriptionId for the update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a subscription record as a user who is not the owner and not an admin. The test should confirm that unauthorized users are denied access to modify other's subscriptions. Setup involves creating a member, a subscription, and then authenticating as a different member before attempting the update. Expect a permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Create both the subscription owner and the unauthorized member.
Create a subscription as the first member.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a subscription with an invalid payload, for instance, using an unsupported notification method or omitting required fields. The test confirms that the endpoint enforces validation and rejects schema-invalid updates with clear error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to allow subscription creation.
Create a valid subscription for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can permanently delete a user's subscription entry by its ID. This scenario validates that subscriptions are fully removed from the system and no longer retrievable. Steps: create a member and a subscription; as admin, call delete and confirm response status and absence from listing. Audit log dependency should be noted for compliance verification.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a new member to assign a subscription for deletion.
Create a new subscription as admin, extract subscriptionId for delete.

scenarios.draft: Member deletes their own subscription, removing all future notifications for the associated topic or thread. Validate that after deletion, the subscription no longer appears in the listing and that only the subscription owner (or admin) can perform this action. Attempting to delete as a non-owner member should be denied.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new board member to hold the subscription.
Create a subscription for that member, then perform delete.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated member can retrieve their own notifications. Steps: (1) Register a member and simulate actions that generate notifications (e.g., creating a subscription and triggering an event such as reply or mention) (2) List notifications and confirm that new notifications related to the member's subscriptions or activities are present and paginated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will own notifications.
Create a subscription for the member to generate notification context.
Admin generates a notification for the member, to later verify presence in notification list.

scenarios.draft: Test that a newly registered member with no notifications receives an empty paginated list when accessing their notification index. Ensures correct handling of empty states and no extraneous errors for zero-notification scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member with no activity to test empty notification retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test a member's ability to perform advanced filtering on their notifications: filter by type (e.g., mention, reply, system), delivery status, or unread status. Generate multiple notifications with different types/statuses, then use PATCH to retrieve filtered lists and validate correct pagination and filtering.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to generate and search notifications for.
Admin creates notifications of various types for the member; these will be used as filter targets.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve a paginated list of all system notices, regardless of active/inactive/scheduled status. First, ensure that there are system notices with different statuses: active, inactive, scheduled for the future, and expired. The test should check that all such notices (including future and expired) are visible to a moderator, verify correct pagination, and confirm that each returned notice contains all required metadata fields (category linkage, title, body, status, activation window, timestamps).

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices in various states: active, inactive, expired, and scheduled future, to ensure all status types are covered for the moderator's view.

scenarios.draft: Test that category-based filtering and pagination work for the moderator system notices listing. First, create a system notice associated with a specific category and others that are global. The test should call the GET endpoint with filtering (if query parameters supported), and verify category-specific and global notices are correctly returned and paginated, including scenarios where there are enough notices to trigger multiple pages.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one notice linked to a specific category and several global notices to verify category-filtering and pagination behaviors.
Create a category in the board to use as the parent for category-limited notices.

scenarios.draft: Test that, as a guest (non-authenticated user), only public, currently active, scheduled system notices are returned, and sensitive or inactive notices are not. Create a mix of active, inactive, scheduled, and expired notices. Access the GET endpoint as a guest and verify only public, currently active/scheduled notices are returned and others are filtered out.

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices in all relevant statuses for validation against expected guest visibility.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can search system notices using advanced filters such as status (active/inactive), scheduled windows (start_at/end_at), and text matching on title or body. Set up a variety of notices with different activation windows and statuses. Perform PATCH search queries that target each filter condition. Confirm that the returned paginated list matches criteria accurately, and out-of-range or no-match queries return empty results.

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices in various statuses and scheduled intervals to match multiple filter criteria.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that moderators can use text search and category-based filters when searching system notices. Create several system notices, some global and some tied to categories, with diverse titles and body content. Issue a PATCH search filtering by keywords and category_id, and validate results include only matching notices. Test negative scenarios where search criteria return no results.

dependencies.purpose: Create a diverse set of system notices for search and filtering tests.
Create categories to use as parents for category-specific notices.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve details for any system notice, regardless of whether it is active, inactive, expired, or scheduled for the future. Create notices with each of these statuses, then invoke the GET endpoint for each notice's ID. Verify that all fields (including category linkage, scheduling, status, and all timestamps) are present and correctly represent the stored values. Check handling of valid and non-existent IDs (404 error expected).

dependencies.purpose: Create one active, one inactive, one scheduled, and one expired system notice to be used for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Verify a moderator can fetch full details for system notices that are inactive or scheduled (not public), as well as active ones. Create a system notice in each state (active, inactive, scheduled, expired), then fetch each individually using the moderator GET endpoint and confirm all attributes are shown. Also check that requesting a non-existent notice ID returns a not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create system notices across all relevant statuses to test visibility for a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve all attachments for an existing comment created by a member. First, create a member and have them create a comment on an existing post. Add one or more attachments to the comment. Then, as an admin, fetch the attachments for the comment and ensure all added files are present with correct metadata (file name, MIME type, uploader, timestamp).

dependencies.purpose: Create a member user who will author the comment.
Create a new comment on an existing post as the member. Requires valid post and member IDs.
Attach one or more files to the comment to ensure there are records to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Verify that fetching attachments for a non-existent (invalid UUID) comment as an admin returns a not found error. This ensures proper error handling and prevents data leaks.
Validate that an unauthorized user (non-admin) cannot access the list of attachments for a comment that belongs to another user, ensuring access control policies are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create two member accounts to simulate unrelated user access.
One user creates a comment, and another tries to access its attachments via the admin endpoint, which should raise permission errors for non-admins.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can filter their comment's attachments using filters such as file name, uploader, and MIME type. Add several attachments with varying properties and then perform filtered searches. Verify correct pagination and filtering is applied as per input.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member.
Upload several attachments for complex filtering and paging tests.

scenarios.draft: Ensure the search API for comment attachments supports correct pagination and sorting. Add more files than the default page size, use pagination parameters, and confirm the results respect both limits and sorting orders.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member.
Upload more attachments than the typical page size to test pagination and sorting.

scenarios.draft: Validate that a member who is not the comment's author cannot search attachments for a comment they do not own. As one member, attempt to run the search API for another member's comment; the API should deny access.

dependencies.purpose: Create two distinct member users.
First member creates a comment. Second member attempts to search its attachments.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that a moderator can search and filter attachments for any comment, regardless of ownership. Moderators should be able to use all filtering options (uploader, MIME type, file name, date) to audit and review attachments across the board.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and moderator user.
Member creates a comment with attachments.
Upload attachments to the member comment.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can perform filtered, paginated searches on attachments for any comment, validating both correct filter application and that no attachments are visible from restricted, non-existent, or unauthorized comments. Ensure security and privacy policies are correctly implemented.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and an admin account.
The member creates comments with varying numbers of attachments.
Upload attachments with differing MIME types, names, and uploaders.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that a comment owner can retrieve full metadata details for a specific attachment on their comment. The metadata must include the file URI, file name, MIME type, uploader ID, and timestamps, confirming all information was stored correctly upon upload.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment as a member.
Upload an attachment to the comment to acquire a valid attachment ID.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that a member who is not the comment's owner cannot access details of attachments belonging to another user's comment. The system should deny access and return the correct error code to prevent unauthorized data exposure.

dependencies.purpose: Create two member users.
First member creates a comment with attachments.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch details for an attachment using an invalid or non-related attachmentId. The API should return an error specifying that the attachment does not exist or does not belong to the given comment, verifying referential integrity enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member for which attachments are referenced.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching notification details for a notificationId when the requesting user is the recipient. First, create a member and trigger a notification (e.g., via post reply or by direct notification using the admin/notification creation endpoint). Attempt to fetch the notification using the recipient's session and confirm that all detailed fields are returned, including message, type, status, delivery/read timestamps, and context as per the schema. The business rule ensuring recipient-only access must be validated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification event for a specific member to ensure there is a notificationId to retrieve. This sets up the context for access control and data presence.

scenarios.draft: Test that a notification cannot be retrieved by a user who is not the recipient. First, create two distinct member accounts and generate a notification for only one of them. Attempt to access the notification's details as a different member and verify that access is denied with the proper error response (e.g., 403/404), ensuring strict privacy and business rule enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create the notification for the first member to be used in the access control test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new notification event for a member by an admin. The admin provides all required fields: recipient member ID, content message, type (reply, mention, etc.), delivery status, and optional context. Verify that the notification is correctly saved, associated with the correct recipient, and that audit logs would be updated. Validate that only allowed roles (admin) can create notifications via this endpoint.

Test creation of a notification using an invalid or non-existent member ID. Verify that the creation fails with a proper error message, and that no notification is generated in the database. Check for system audit of failed attempts and that there are no side effects.

Verify that a moderator can successfully create a notification for a member. Supply valid member ID, content, type, and delivery parameters. Check that the notification is persisted, assigned to the correct recipient, and that the moderator's identity is appropriately recorded in audit trails. Access must only be granted for authorized roles.

Attempt to create a notification using this endpoint with a role that is neither moderator nor admin. Ensure that access is denied, and an appropriate authorization error is returned, confirming that business logic restricts creation accordingly.

Test that a member can mark their own notification as read using this endpoint. After creating a notification (using admin or moderator creation endpoint), call this update as the recipient. Confirm that the notification's read_at timestamp updates, status reflects the change, and audit log (if visible) records the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create the notification for the recipient member to enable the update scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member cannot update a notification that does not belong to them. Create a notification for one member, then attempt to perform the update as a different member. Expect an error response (403/404), verifying strict recipient-only update rights for notifications.

dependencies.purpose: Generate a notification assigned to another member for update access test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can update notification properties for any recipient. This may include marking as read, updating the message content, changing delivery status, or addressing delivery failure. Create a notification, then as admin, perform various allowed updates and verify the persisted changes. Audit logging should reflect the admin action, and system integrity must be maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification as the basis for admin update actions.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to perform an update as admin on a non-existent notificationId. Ensure the operation fails with a not-found error and check that no accidental record or system side effect is introduced by the invalid update attempt.

Verify that a moderator can view the detailed metadata of a specific attachment linked to a comment. Scenario: Create a member, create a comment under a post, upload an attachment as the member, then use moderator privileges to retrieve this attachment's metadata using its attachmentId and associated commentId. Confirm all metadata (file name, URI, uploader, mime type, timestamps) matches expected input. This checks correct role-based read access and the referential integrity of attachment metadata for moderation.

dependencies.purpose: Create/register a new board member (the original uploader/author of the attachment).
Create a new comment as the registered member so that an attachment can be linked to it.
Upload a new file attachment to the comment created above; returns attachmentId and associates metadata.

scenarios.draft: Test the case where a moderator attempts to retrieve details for a non-existent attachmentId under a valid commentId. After creating a comment as a member, attempt to fetch with a random (non-existent) attachmentId and expect a 404 not found error. This ensures proper error handling and no information leakage about deleted or unknown files.

dependencies.purpose: Create/register a new member (comment/post owner).
Create a test comment to produce a valid commentId for testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that unauthorized users (such as non-owners, non-moderators, or guests) cannot view the detailed metadata of an attachment on a comment that is not theirs. This checks role-based access control enforcement for sensitive or private attachments.

dependencies.purpose: Register a legitimate board member (as the attachment owner).
Let the owner create a comment for attachment upload.
Owner uploads attachment to the comment.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin user can retrieve detailed information about a comment attachment, regardless of who uploaded the file. Scenario: Register a new member, create a comment as that member, have them upload an attachment, then access the attachment detail as admin. Checks for correct access and metadata integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member who will upload the attachment.
Member creates a comment for attachment.
Upload the attachment (to be accessed as admin).

scenarios.draft: Test the case where an admin requests an attachmentId that does not exist under a comment. After registering a member and creating their comment, try a random UUID as attachmentId and assert that a 404 or not found error is returned. Verifies proper not-found error handling and no leakage of metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Add a test board member.
Create a comment to act as a valid context.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that if a regular member attempts to retrieve an attachment not owned by them (without admin privileges), the request is denied. This tests enforcement of strict access control for viewing attachment metadata at the admin path.

dependencies.purpose: Register both an uploader (owner) and a second, non-owner member.
Owner creates comment for attachment.
Owner uploads an attachment linked to their comment.

scenarios.draft: A registered member adds a valid file attachment to their own comment. Scenario: Register a member, create a comment, upload an allowed file type via this endpoint, and verify the returned metadata matches input (file name, MIME type, uploader ID, URI). Confirms attachment is linked to the comment and retrievable by the member.

dependencies.purpose: Register new member for attachment upload.
Create a comment using the registered member.

scenarios.draft: Try to upload a file attachment as a member to a non-existent commentId. Expects a 404 or error response, verifying the system does not allow orphaned attachments and checks for valid foreign key constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare an authenticated member for request.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member cannot add attachments to another member's comment. Register two members; one creates a comment, and the second attempts to add an attachment to it. Request should be denied (forbidden) and logged as an unauthorized action.

dependencies.purpose: Register both owner and secondary member users.
Let owner create the target comment.

scenarios.draft: Test business rules on allowed file types: attempt to add a file with a disallowed MIME type or extension, and verify that the operation fails with a clear error. Confirms that server-side content-type validation prevents unsupported formats (e.g., blocked executables or scripts).

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a member for attachment upload testing.
Create a member's comment to hold attachments.

scenarios.draft: Verify the moderator can add an attachment to any comment (including comments not owned by them): register a member, create a comment as a member, then add an attachment as moderator. Checks cross-role assignment and audit capturing. Response should confirm correct association of metadata and permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user to act as comment author.
Create a comment with the member's credentials.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to add an attachment to a non-existent commentId as a moderator. Should receive an error (not found), verifying the system enforces valid parent comment existence for all uploads regardless of role.

Try to upload a file with a blocked/unsupported MIME type as a moderator. Validates moderation interface is subject to the same file validation logic as member uploader, denying non-compliant file formats.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a target comment exists by registering a member author.
Member creates a comment to serve as upload parent.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can upload and associate an attachment with any comment—even if not the original author—bypassing member-level restrictions. Register a member, have the member create a comment, then perform the upload as admin. Validate that response metadata is correct and that audit information records the admin as uploader.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member (acts as comment author).
Comment created by member for admin to upload against.

scenarios.draft: Admin attempts to upload an attachment to a non-existent commentId. Expect a not found or error response. Verifies admin interface applies required referential checks, no matter the user role.

Admin attempts to upload a restricted file type; ensure upload is rejected and error message is returned. Confirms that even admin uploads are restricted by security/content validation logic for attachment file types.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to ensure a valid target comment exists.
Valid comment is created by member, with admin acting as uploader.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a board member's audit or registration data by an admin. First, ensure a valid member exists by creating a member record. As an admin, perform a PUT request with updated suspension status (e.g., setting the suspended_at field), join time correction, or user_identifier change. Confirm that the response reflects the updated fields and includes proper audit logging. Validate that only allowed fields are updated and that the member's record is otherwise unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member record to be used as the target for the update scenario, ensuring there is a valid memberId.

scenarios.draft: Test update failure when an admin tries to update a member using an invalid or non-existent memberId. Attempt a PUT with a random or malformed UUID as the memberId path parameter. Expect the system to return a not-found error, and no changes should occur in the database. The scenario validates proper error handling for not-found resources.

Test that update attempts by users without admin privileges are denied. Attempt to update another user's member record as a non-admin (e.g., as a member or guest). The API should respond with a permission-denied error, and audit logs should capture the attempted violation. No changes should be made to the member record.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a test member record to target for the invalid-permission update.

scenarios.draft: Test update failure due to invalid input data. Provide a request body that violates schema constraints—for example, missing required updatable fields, providing null for non-nullable fields, or invalid data types. The system should return a validation error, and the member record should remain unchanged in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a member to be used in the invalid update request, ensuring there's a real memberId.

scenarios.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a membership record by admin. Begin by creating a new member with admin role, then request DELETE with the member's id. Verify that the record is completely removed from the system (hard delete), no longer appears in queries, and any attempt to fetch the deleted record returns not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member record to serve as the target for deletion and ensure valid test context.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when attempting to delete a non-existent or random UUID as memberId. The system should respond with a not-found error and ensure there are no unintended deletions or changes to other member records.

Test that only admins can delete member records. Attempt deletion by a non-admin user and confirm that permission is denied, the database is unchanged, and an audit event is logged regarding the failed attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a member record for the deletion test, targeting enforcement of role-based permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of the full guest session list as an admin. Ensure that there are one or more guest records in the system—if not, create guest sessions beforehand. Send a GET request and verify the complete list of guest session objects matches those stored. The test should confirm all required fields are present in the response and that only admins can view all data.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more guest session records to ensure the system under test has retrievable guest data.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that non-admin users (guests, members, moderators) cannot access the guest session list via the admin endpoint. Attempt to retrieve the list as a non-admin and expect an access-denied response. Confirm there is no data leakage of guest analytics to unauthorized users.

Test the system's response when no guest records exist. As an admin, request the guest session list on an empty database. The response should be a valid but empty list, and no error should occur. This validates system behavior under an empty dataset.

Test successful advanced search and filtering over guest sessions as admin. First, create several guest session records with varying first_seen and last_seen timestamps, and session_identifiers. Issue a PATCH request with valid filters (by session_identifier or date range). Validate that only matching guest sessions are returned and results are correctly paginated and sorted as per request.

dependencies.purpose: Insert multiple guest sessions with varying field values to serve as search/filter test data.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for malformed or invalid filter parameters. Send a PATCH search request with invalid field names, values out of range, or incorrect types. Validate that the system responds with a validation or error message and no guest session records are returned.

Verify that non-admin roles cannot perform advanced searches over guest analytics. Attempt to PATCH search as a guest, member, or moderator and confirm that an appropriate permission-denied error is returned.

Test retrieving a guest session by its unique guestId. First, create a guest record, then fetch it by its id as an admin. Confirm the returned data includes the full detail for the correct guest session, and the fields match what was inserted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test guest session to be used for the targeted fetch operation, ensuring the existence of a valid guestId.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling for attempts to fetch a guest session with a random or invalid UUID. Issue a GET request using a non-existent or malformed guestId and confirm the system responds with a not-found error and no data is inadvertently returned.

Check that only admins can access guest session details using this endpoint. Attempt access as a non-admin, and confirm an access-denied error is received and no guest session information is revealed.

Test that a member can successfully retrieve the full details of an active, public system notice by its UUID using this endpoint. First, ensure that a system notice is created and marked as active by an admin. Then, as a member, attempt to fetch the notice via its UUID. Validate that all expected fields (title, body, category association, status, scheduling) are present in the response and correspond to the persisted data. Ensure that public and currently active status is respected, making the notice visible to members. Edge case: try to fetch a non-existent notice and verify that an appropriate 404 or error message is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active system notice as data setup, since only admins can create notices.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member cannot retrieve a system notice that is inactive, expired, or scheduled for the future. First, create a notice as inactive or with scheduling outside the current date. Attempt to fetch the notice as a member and expect an error or appropriate denial indicating insufficient visibility. Confirm that only eligible active notices are accessible through this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create an inactive or scheduled (future) system notice to be tested for visibility restrictions.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully create a new system notice with valid fields (title, body, is_active, and optional category/scheduling). Check that the response includes a generated UUID, timestamps, and correct association with any referenced category. Validate that the created notice is retrievable by ID and visible according to its is_active/schedule settings.

Test failure when attempting to create a notice with a category_id that does not exist. The system should reject the creation and return a clear error message about the invalid category reference. Validate that no new notice is created in this case.

Test creation logic enforcing uniqueness of notice titles within the same category. First, create a notice with a specific title under a category. Then attempt to create another notice with the same title in the same category. Expect a validation error about duplicate title. Changing the category or title should allow creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the initial system notice to set up a duplicate title error in the same category.

scenarios.draft: Verify an admin can update an existing system notice by its UUID, modifying fields such as title, body, status, scheduling, and associated category. The notice should reflect the updated values on retrieval and in subsequent listings. Validate correct audit logging (if exposed) and ensure all field-level validation (e.g., valid schedule logic, unique title per category) applies.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system notice to be updated in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test the failure scenario where an admin attempts to update a system notice with an invalid scheduling window (start_at after end_at). The API should reject the update and return a validation error specifying the scheduling logic violation. Ensure the original notice fields remain unchanged after the failed operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system notice as a prerequisite for testing a schedule validation error.

scenarios.draft: Validate that an admin can successfully delete an existing system notice using its UUID. First, create a system notice to ensure a known record exists. Then perform the DELETE and verify the notice is no longer retrievable by ID. Confirm that deletion is irreversible and is audit-logged (if possible). Try retrieving the deleted notice and expect a 404 or not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the system notice that will be deleted in this scenario.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full paginated list of currently registered and historical administrators. The response should include all necessary metadata (UUID, user_identifier, grant/revoke timestamps) without any sensitive or extraneous data. Confirm that revoked (inactive) and currently active admins are both included, and no filtering/sorting is applied by default.

Test the result when no admin records exist in the system—expected result is an empty array or correct pagination metadata. Precondition: System has no admin records, or all have been deleted for the purpose of this test.
Check that a request to list all admins from a user without administrative privileges (e.g., a regular member or guest) is rejected with a clear permission error and no admin data is leaked.

Test that a member cannot retrieve a system notice that is inactive, expired, or scheduled for the future. First, create a notice as inactive or with scheduling outside the current date. Attempt to fetch the notice as a member and expect an error or appropriate denial indicating insufficient visibility. Confirm that only eligible active notices are accessible through this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create an inactive or scheduled (future) system notice to be tested for visibility restrictions.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member who created a topic can successfully update its core fields such as title, description, category, and pinned/closed state by providing all valid and unique data. The process begins by creating a member, a valid and active category, and then creating a topic under that category by the member. The member then issues an update request to change one or more allowed fields, and the test verifies that the topic reflects all intended changes and a successful response is returned. Authorizations and unique-field validations must pass for the update to succeed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member who will act as topic creator.
Create an active discussion category under which the topic can be created.
Create a new topic as the member, establishing ownership for update permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to update a topic's title to a value that already exists within the same category. First, create a member and a category. Then, create two topics within this category. Attempt to update the second topic's title to the first topic's title. The operation should fail due to the uniqueness constraint on topic titles within a category, and the API must return a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member for topic creation.
Set up a category in which duplicate title constraint will be tested.
Create two topics in the same category with unique initial titles.

scenarios.draft: Test that a regular member who is not the topic creator cannot update a topic. After creating a topic with one member, attempt to update the topic using the identity of a different member. The API must reject the update with an authorization error, ensuring only the owner/authorized roles have update rights.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members: one as topic creator, one as attempted updater.
Establish a category for the topic.
Create the topic with the first member (assigning ownership).

scenarios.draft: Test failure when a member tries to move a topic to a categoryId that does not exist or is inactive. First, set up a valid member, create a topic in a valid category, and attempt to update the topic with an invalid or inactive category ID. The system should reject the update, returning an appropriate error indicating the category constraint violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member (topic owner).
Create at least one valid category for initial topic creation.
Create the topic to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully update any topic’s fields, including title, description, category, and state, regardless of ownership. Begin by creating a member, a moderator, a category, and a topic. The moderator performs an update on a topic they do not own. The operation should succeed, demonstrating moderator privilege.

dependencies.purpose: Create a regular member to act as topic creator.
Create a moderator user with update privileges.
Set up at least one category for topic creation.
Create a topic by the member, so the moderator can update it.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator’s update attempt with invalid fields—such as duplicate title in a category or non-existent category—fails. Set up a scenario where the moderator tries to assign a duplicate title or invalid category to a topic. The test verifies that appropriate business rule validations trigger error responses and prevent the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will own the initial topics.
Register a moderator for privileged access.
Create one or more categories for testing invalid values.
Create two topics in the same category, and attempt to update one with a duplicate title.

scenarios.draft: Validate that an admin can update any topic in the system, regardless of ownership, including changing titles, descriptions, categories, and state. The process sets up a member, an admin, a category, and a topic. The admin updates the topic’s details, and the test confirms changes are correctly applied, indicating admin privilege.

dependencies.purpose: Create the original topic creator as a regular member.
Register an admin user for privileged operations.
Create a category for the topic.
Insert a topic in the system for the admin to update.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when an admin attempts to update a topic’s title to a non-unique value (already taken within the category). After member and topic setup, an admin tries to rename a topic to another topic’s title under the same category. The operation must fail with a uniqueness violation, and the appropriate error message returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for topic ownership.
Register an admin for management operations.
Set up the category in which the uniqueness constraint is enforced.
Create two topics with unique initial titles for subsequent duplicate title testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully delete (hard delete) a topic, causing the topic and all cascade-dependent entities to be removed from the database. The scenario involves creating a member, a moderator, a category, and a topic, then having the moderator issue the delete request. The operation should return a success response, and subsequent read requests for the topic must result in not found errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for topic ownership.
Register a moderator for deletion privileges.
Set up an active category.
Create the topic to be deleted by the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test the error flow when a moderator attempts to delete a topic that does not exist or has already been deleted. The moderator issues a delete request for an invalid or previously erased topic ID. The system should respond with a not found error, confirming correct error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a moderator role is prepared for operation.

scenarios.draft: Test that a regular member without moderator privileges is not able to delete topics. The test sets up a member and a topic, and then attempts to perform a deletion as a member user rather than as a moderator. The API should reject the request with an authorization error, ensuring access control and security policies are respected.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member (non-moderator) who will attempt the unauthorized delete.
Create the topic's category.
Create the topic under the member's identity.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully hard delete a topic, permanently removing it and related entities from the database. The test creates a member, an admin, a category, and a topic, followed by the admin performing the delete operation. Afterwards, attempts to fetch the topic should result in not found, confirming full deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to own the topic.
Register an admin with delete privileges.
Set up a valid category for topic creation.
Create a topic for subsequent deletion by the admin.

scenarios.draft: Validate error handling when an admin attempts to delete a topic that does not exist or was previously deleted. The API should return a not found response, ensuring data integrity and robust error handling for repeated or invalid delete operations.

dependencies.purpose: Set up an admin account for operation.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully delete a thread from a topic. This test requires that a topic and thread exist, and that the user performing the deletion has admin privileges. The expected outcome is that the thread, along with all associated posts, is permanently removed from the system, and subsequent attempts to access it result in a 'not found' error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic as a prerequisite for thread creation and deletion.
Create a thread under the topic before attempting to delete it.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that attempting to delete a non-existent thread by admin returns a 404 error. The admin should receive an appropriate error message, and no system data should be changed. This is important to test the error handling for invalid UUIDs.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic to use for referencing when using a non-existent thread ID.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to perform a thread deletion operation as a non-admin user (e.g., as a guest or a regular member), and verify that the API returns a permission-denied error. Confirm that the thread remains in place after the failed attempt and no data is lost or changed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic for the thread belonging to.
Create a thread as target for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member can retrieve a paginated list of all current (non-deleted) posts in a specified thread. Ensure that posts created by different members are visible, provided they are not soft-deleted. The test should check proper pagination, sorting order, and access rights for the authenticated member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic so that a thread can be created within it.
Create a thread for which posts will be retrieved.
Create several posts under the thread to exercise pagination and retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Check the system's response when listing posts in a valid thread that has no posts. The response should be a paginated list containing zero items, and there should be no error. This ensures correct handling of empty thread situations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic as a parent for the thread.
Create a thread with no posts.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to access the post list of a thread as a guest or unauthenticated user and verify that the system blocks access, returning an authentication-required or permission-denied error. This tests access control and confidentiality for member-only content.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic and thread as a member to use for permission testing.
Create a thread with posts as a member.
Populate the thread with at least one post to have data to protect.

scenarios.draft: Given a thread with multiple posts, test that a member can search for posts containing specific keywords in their content and receive only the relevant subset of posts. This validates the effectiveness of full-text search and filtering mechanics on post content.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic for the thread.
Create a thread for post insertion and search.
Create multiple posts with varying content for realistic keyword searches.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that searching for posts within a thread supports pagination parameters, returning the correct subset and navigation hints for the overall result set size. This test requires enough posts to deliberately trigger pagination, and should validate result count, page info, and sort order.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic to place a thread in.
Create a thread for post creation.
Add sufficient posts to test multi-page response to search.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search for posts in a thread using malformed or invalid search criteria (for example, an unsupported filter or incorrect field type). The expected result is a clear error response without corrupting data or returning results. This covers business validation of filtering logic and type checking.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic as parent for the thread.
Insert a thread that will be searched.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a member can retrieve complete details of a specific post within a thread, including all allowable fields (body, creator, timestamps, metadata). This tests normal drilldown for a thread's post by ID and checks permissions and correct field population.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic for threaded discussion.
Create a thread where posts can be made.
Create a post in the thread to be retrieved by its ID.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to fetch a post using a valid thread ID but a non-existent post ID, and verify that a 404 or not-found error is returned. This scenario ensures robust error handling for invalid UUIDs and resource references.

dependencies.purpose: Create topic and thread for basis of a valid thread context.
Create a thread with no post matching the target post ID.

scenarios.draft: Verify that attempts to get details of posts in a restricted or private thread by an unauthorized user are blocked, returning the proper error response. This protects content privacy against unauthorized access attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic and thread with restricted access (simulate member-only state).
Insert a thread with member-only visibility.
Create a post for privacy validation.

scenarios.draft: Test that an authenticated member can create a new post in a thread by supplying valid data. Upon success, the newly created post should be returned with all details, and subsequent retrieval of the thread's post list should include the new post.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic so that a thread can be created for posting.
Insert a thread in which posts can be created.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a post in a thread that has been administratively closed to new posts. The API should reject the request with a clear error indicating the thread's status does not permit posting, and no post should be created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic for thread creation.
Create a thread and have it administratively closed for posting before the test.

scenarios.draft: Try to create a post in an existing thread as a guest (unauthenticated) user, and verify that an authentication-required or permission-denied error is returned. No post should be created, and only members should have posting privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a topic for thread creation.
Create a thread which is the target for guest post attempt.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a thread post owner (authenticated member) can successfully update their own post's content. Steps: Register a new member, create a thread under a topic, make an initial post, then update the post's body and is_edited status. Ensure the change is reflected, all business rules (editable fields only) are respected, and an audit trail is updated if required. The outcome should be the complete, updated post details returned by the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create/register a new board member that will act as the post/thread creator.
Create a discussion topic as the post's parent context.
Create a thread in the topic for posting (requires member session and valid topicId).
Create a new post under the thread by the member, which will later be updated in the test.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that a non-owner member cannot update another user's post. Scenario: Register two members, have one of them create a thread and a post. The other member attempts to update the post and is denied (unauthorized/forbidden error). The system must block the update attempt and return an appropriate error message. Only moderators or admins (not covered here) may override this restriction per business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first member who will create a thread and initial post.
Create a second member who will attempt the unauthorized update.
Create a discussion topic for posting.
Create a thread in the topic using the first member's credentials.
Create a post under the thread by the first member.

scenarios.draft: Test that updates with invalid input (such as empty or excessively long body, or invalid non-editable fields in payload) are rejected. A member creates a post and tries to update it with invalid body content or attempts to update restricted fields. The system must return validation errors and keep the original post unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member for post creation and update actions.
Create a valid topic for the new thread.
Create a thread for post insertion.
Create the post which will be updated with invalid data.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to update a post using a non-existent threadId or postId. The system should return a not-found or resource error, indicating the referenced entities do not exist. This guards against ID spoofing or race conditions.

Verify that the post creator (member) can soft-delete their own post by marking it deleted (deleted_at field set). Scenario: Register a member, create a thread, create a post, then soft-delete it. After the call, the post should not be shown in regular lists to typical users. All actions must be audit-logged. Attempting to delete again should result in error or be idempotent per business rule.

dependencies.purpose: Register a board member for thread/post creation.
Create a topic in which to test thread/post flows.
Create a thread as soft-deletion requires real parent context.
Create a post to be soft-deleted by its creator.

scenarios.draft: Verify that non-owners cannot delete posts they do not own. Register two members, have the first member create a post, then attempt to soft-delete it with the credentials of the second member. The operation must fail with a permission error and the post must remain visible.

dependencies.purpose: Register the first member to create the post.
Register a second member for unauthorized delete attempt.
Create a topic for thread and post creation.
Create a thread for post insertion.
Create a post by the first member to be targeted for delete by the second.

scenarios.draft: Ensure an error is returned when attempting to delete a post with an invalid or non-existent threadId or postId. The system should handle this gracefully and not affect existing records.

Verify that the owner of a post can retrieve the complete list of all version snapshots for that post. Scenario: A member creates a post, performs one or more edits (causing versioning), then fetches version history. Confirm versions are complete, in correct order, and include all required fields (version number, content snapshot, editor ID, created_at).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will own the post and perform edits.
Create a topic for member posting.
Insert a thread where the post will be created.
Create the initial post.
Create one or more new post versions (edits) for version history testing.

scenarios.draft: Test the behavior when a non-owner member attempts to retrieve versions for a post they do not own. If the business logic restricts access, a forbidden/authorization error must occur. If moderators/admins may view, ensure member access is denied but role-based access works accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Register the member who owns the post.
Register a second member to attempt unauthorized version list retrieval.
Create a topic.
Create a thread in the topic.
Make a post as the first member.
Create an edit/version for the post.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve post versions for a non-existent postId. The API should clearly indicate a not-found or domain error, and no data should be returned.

Check that a post owner can search/filter version history using advanced query parameters (e.g., by editor, version number, or date range). Scenario: A member creates and edits their post several times, then searches for specific versions using allowed filters, confirming only matching versions are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for post and editing actions.
Establish a topic for the thread/post.
Insert a thread.
Initial post insertion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search the post's version history with invalid or malformed filter parameters (e.g., non-existent editor ID, invalid version number range, or improper pagination). The API should return a validation error, helpful response, or empty result as per business rule.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for post and versions.
Create a topic for thread/post flow.
Create a thread.
Make a post to be versioned.
Create at least one version for the test post.

scenarios.draft: Try to use the advanced version search endpoint on a non-existent postId. The system must return a not-found error and not expose any data.

Test that a member (post owner) can fetch a specific version of their post by versionId. The response should precisely match the expected version content, editor, and created_at. Steps: Member creates a post, edits it to produce one or more versions, and requests to fetch a specific version using the returned versionId values in version listing.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for posting and version testing.
Create a parent topic.
Create a thread for posting.
Create a post to be edited (versioned).
Create multiple versions (edits) of the post.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a non-owner member cannot fetch post version snapshots of another user's post if business logic restricts such access. If applicable, a forbidden error is expected. Set up two members: one creates the post and versions, the other attempts to fetch a version snapshot by versionId.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post owner/member.

Post creation.

scenarios.draft: Try to fetch a post version using a non-existent versionId or for a non-existent postId. The API must return an appropriate not-found error and not expose any version data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who owns the comment and its version.

Confirm the full version content and that all edit metadata are visible, covering audit and compliance requirements.

The system should return a not found error, validating error handling for missing or already-purged version records.

As the authenticated comment author, submit a new version with updated content. Confirm the version is appended, version numbering is correct, and the new content is visible in history. Ensures normal member edit and revision workflow functions as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will author the comment.

Set up two distinct members, let the first create a comment, and then attempt to create a version as the second member. Expect a permission denied error, validating enforcement of author-only versioning for members, supporting editing security.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a version (edit) for a comment as a moderator. Set up by creating a member and their comment, then perform an edit through the moderator role. The new version should appear in the version list, update all relevant fields, and not alter the version sequence in unexpected ways. Verifies moderator editing power, audit logging, and revision management.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as the original comment author to ensure comment ownership.
Initial comment by member to provide an editable entity for moderation.

scenarios.draft: Test that creating a comment version using a nonexistent commentId as a moderator results in a not found error. This checks for proper error reporting and data consistency on attempted moderation of invalid or deleted entity references.

The version should appear correctly in the version history, have admin as editor, and reflect changes in both content and audit metadata—demonstrating administrative override and compliance audit support.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as a test comment author.
