scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a comment version as admin with invalid content (e.g., empty or exceeding allowed length), expecting the system to reject with a validation error. This checks that business rules for content integrity and field constraints are enforced even for admin users.

dependencies.purpose: Provision the initial member as actual comment creator.
Insert the comment to be versioned and supply invalid new content as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a detailed report record with a valid reportId as a user with moderator privileges. Scenario: Create a report as a member, capture its reportId, then as a moderator, fetch full detail to ensure all expected fields and sensitive information are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderation report as a member and obtain its reportId to be used for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a report with a non-existent reportId as a moderator, expecting a not-found error. Prepare the moderation role context and issue a GET request using a fake or deleted UUID, verifying the response is an appropriate error object.

Test access denied for users without moderator or admin privileges when attempting to get a report's details. Create a standard member user, attempt to fetch a report by ID, and verify the system returns a permission error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a report as a member so an unauthorized member may try to access it, provoking a forbidden/permission denied error.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving a detailed report as an admin using a valid reportId. Create a report as a member, then use the admin role to request the report details, verifying receipt of all content including sensitive metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Submit a moderation report as a member and capture the reportId for admin retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to retrieve a report with an invalid/non-existent reportId as an admin. Issue the GET request with a bogus ID and confirm the system returns a not-found error.

Test the successful flow for a member creating a new report against abusive or inappropriate content. Prepare an authenticated member, make sure the target content (post or comment) exists, and submit a valid report. Verify the report is persisted and returned with correct status and details.

Test that double-reporting of the same content by the same member is prevented as per business rules. As a member, submit a report on a target entity, then attempt to submit another report against the same target. The API should block the duplicate and return an appropriate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Submit the first report to set up double-reporting scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test handling submission of a report referencing non-existent content. Attempt to report a post/comment using a fabricated or deleted resource id; the system should return an error for invalid reference.
Test that unauthenticated users (guests) are forbidden from creating reports. As a guest, try to submit a report and verify the API responds with an authorization required or forbidden error.

Test that a user with moderator role can create a moderation report successfully, e.g., to escalate peer content or flag rule violations. Prepare moderator authentication and a valid content reference, then create the report. Verify response and data integrity.

Test the successful creation of a moderation report as an admin, confirming admins can file reports directly (such as when identifying policy issues or acting on complaints). Verify the report is properly persisted and returned with admin metadata.

Test successful deletion of a notification as the notification's recipient. The user should be able to remove a notification they own from their notification feed. First, ensure the user is authenticated as a member and has at least one notification (create one if needed using the admin/notification POST endpoint). Attempt to delete the notification using its notificationId and confirm that it is no longer accessible via GET. The system should log the deletion for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for the member to ensure there is a notification to delete. This also validates permissions and setup.
Verify the notification exists before attempting deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a notification by a user who is not the recipient. Attempting to delete another user's notification should be forbidden, and the system must return an appropriate permission-denied error. Create a notification for one member, and authenticate as a different member to attempt the deletion. The attempt should be logged for audit, and the notification must remain accessible to its rightful owner.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for Member A using admin privileges.
Ensure Member B exists for the forbidden attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a notification that does not exist. Attempt to delete a notificationId that is not present in the system (either never existed or was already deleted). The system should return a clear not-found error and must not affect any other data. This ensures proper handling of incorrect identifiers.

Test that an admin can delete a member's notification. First, ensure a notification exists for a member by creating it as admin. Authenticate as an admin user and delete the notification on behalf of the member. The deletion should succeed, be audit-logged, and the notification should be gone for the recipient.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for the member.
Create or authenticate an admin user for the action.
Verify the notification is removed for the recipient after deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can delete their own notification using the admin/notifications DELETE endpoint. First, create a notification assigning the admin as the recipient. Delete that notification as the admin and confirm its removal with a follow-up GET request. System should audit this action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for the admin to enable deletion.
Verify the notification no longer exists after deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can delete a notification belonging to any user (not just themselves). First, create a member and a notification for that member. As admin, attempt to delete the notification. Confirm deletion both as admin and as the affected member, and check audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for notification ownership.
Create a notification for the member.

scenarios.draft: Test that deleting a non-existent notification as an admin returns a not-found error. Attempt to delete a notificationId that does not exist in the database and verify a clear, user-friendly error is returned. Ensure that no side effects occur and audit logging is preserved.

Test that non-admin users are unable to use the admin/notifications DELETE endpoint to delete notifications, even if they own the notification. Attempt to delete a notification as a member through the admin endpoint and expect a forbidden/unauthorized error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a notification for a member for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin is able to successfully retrieve a paginated list of activity logs. Authenticate as an admin, then perform a GET request to /admin/activityLogs and verify the response includes valid log entries with all metadata present. Confirm that pagination metadata is correct and logs reflect various types of actor and action events.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin authentication for access to logs.
Create several activity logs for listing.

scenarios.draft: Test pagination and sorting functionality when listing activity logs. Populate the system with multiple activity logs using POST, then retrieve them using the GET endpoint with pagination parameters. Verify correct ordering, page boundaries, and total count metadata are accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple log entries to test pagination/sorting.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can also retrieve the activity logs list. Authenticate as a moderator, perform the GET request, and verify log content and permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator user for system access.

scenarios.draft: Test that members or guests are denied access to GET /admin/activityLogs. Attempt to retrieve the logs as a member and as a guest and confirm a forbidden or unauthorized error response, ensuring sensitive audit data is protected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for negative testing.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator can access activity logs through the moderator endpoint. Authenticate as a moderator, retrieve logs, and confirm entries contain expected metadata. Ensure the set includes recent moderator and non-moderator activities.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a moderator.
Log recent activities for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that members or guests cannot access moderator/activityLogs. Attempt to retrieve using member and guest credentials and expect an unauthorized or forbidden response, with appropriate error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for negative access test.

scenarios.draft: Test pagination and completeness of activity logs returned for a large dataset. Populate with many activity logs, then retrieve several pages via the moderator endpoint, confirming no loss or corruption of data and correct pagination details.

dependencies.purpose: Bulk-generate activity logs for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test searching activity logs with a filter on a specific time interval (e.g., last week). Submit a PATCH request with created_at filters, and confirm that only logs within that range are returned, with accurate metadata. Use admin authentication.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin for search.
Create logs with various timestamps for filtering.

scenarios.draft: Test activity log search filtering by actor_type (e.g., filter for member vs admin actions). Create sample logs for both types, issue a search filter query, and validate response contents only include matching actor types.

dependencies.purpose: Insert logs for multiple actor types for search coverage.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to perform a PATCH search for activity logs using member permissions and confirm that access is denied with a proper error. This verifies security boundaries are enforced for advanced log queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a member for this attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test a search query specifying a time range or criteria with no matching logs. The result should be an empty page but should not be an error. This verifies correct handling of empty searches.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure records exist outside the test filter window.

scenarios.draft: Test the advanced search of engagement statistics by applying valid filter parameters such as specific time ranges, dimension filters (e.g., by topic or segment), and valid pagination settings. The scenario ensures that the result set contains only records that match the criteria and that the pagination boundary conditions (e.g., page size limits, last page) behave as expected. Test with an admin user to ensure proper role access.

dependencies.purpose: Insert at least a few sample engagement stat records to ensure there are matching and non-matching entries for the search filter.

scenarios.draft: Test scenario where an admin attempts to search engagement statistics with malformed or logically invalid query parameters (such as broken date formats, exceedingly large page sizes, or impossible segment values). System must return a clear and user-friendly error message, and no data should be leaked or returned unexpectedly.

Fetch a specific engagement stat by known valid ID as an admin. The system should return the correct detailed record matching the ID. Validate all returned fields and ensure representation matches the persisted record. This is a basic happy path retrieval scenario.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample engagement stat record and take its ID to use for detail retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve an engagement statistic using a nonexistent or invalid ID. The system must return a 404 not found error or equivalent message, and must not leak any data about other records.

Successfully create a new engagement statistics record with all required fields filled according to the schema, using a valid reporting period, dimensions, and count values. The record should be retrievable afterward via the detail and search APIs. This validates positive creation and persistence.

Attempt to create an engagement statistic entry with critical missing or invalid fields (such as omitting period, dimension, or providing negative or non-numeric counts). Verify that the API validates input, rejects the record, and returns suitable error messages for each business rule violation.

Update an existing engagement stat record by changing allowable fields (such as adjusting user activity, post count, or time period). The response should show the updated values, and repeated retrieval should confirm persistence. All business rules for field updates (such as uniqueness, valid ranges) must be enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an engagement stat record to obtain a valid ID for update.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a stat with data that violates schema constraints (such as setting a period that overlaps another stat, using negative counts, or missing required fields). The system must prevent the update and return a clear error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create an original engagement stat record as the basis for attempted invalid update.

scenarios.draft: Delete an existing engagement stat record by its ID as an admin. The deletion must be permanent (as no soft-delete exists), and subsequent retrieval with the same ID should return a 404 not found error. All deletion events must be fully compliant with audit expectations.

dependencies.purpose: Insert a new engagement stat record to acquire a valid ID to be deleted.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete an engagement stat using a nonexistent or already-deleted ID. Must verify that the system returns an appropriate not found or error message, and no unintended effects occur.

Test that an admin user can retrieve the full list of comments on the discussion board, including both active and deleted comments, as authorized by admin privileges. Confirm pagination, expected summary fields, and presence of deletion markers for soft-deleted comments. Validate that sensitive content is appropriately handled. The test requires at least one active and one deleted comment in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member account to generate comments with a known author for visibility in the listing.
Post a topic under which comments can be created and tested.
Post a thread for comments association.
Add a post (parent for comments) so comments can be tested.
Create at least two comments (one to remain active, one to later soft-delete for deletion visibility test).
Soft-delete one of the comments created, marking is_deleted to test listing of deleted comments.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve the complete comment list, covering both active and deleted comments. Confirm that moderation privileges allow the viewing of deleted content, and that sensitive/private information is not exposed beyond the expected comment fields. Check pagination and summary structure. Requires comments present in various states.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member so that comments on the platform can be generated for comprehensive listing.
Provide a discussion topic under which test comments can be made.
Establish a thread for assigning test comments.
Create a parent post to which comments will be attached.
Insert test comments so there is content for the listing, including a comment marked deleted for moderation evaluation.
Convert one comment to deleted state for verification of moderator listing permissions.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can perform advanced searches on comments using filters such as content keywords and date ranges. Validate correct results are returned for simple and compound filters, including paginated results. Make sure only comments within the filtered criteria and within admin's privileges appear. Check for cases with no results as well.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a member to own comments with known content and timestamps for reliable filtering tests.
Create a topic for placing posts and comments.
Add a thread for targeted post and comment operations.
Create a post for attaching comments to, allowing controlled test data creation.
Create multiple comments with distinct known contents and timestamps to be used in search filtering tests.

scenarios.draft: Verify that when an admin searches with filters for a specific member ID and soft-deleted status, the resulting comment list contains only comments written by that member and reflecting their is_deleted status. Validate edge cases of no matching results and pagination across deleted and active comments.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member whose ID will be used as a filter for search queries.
Add a topic for creating context.
Add a thread to use as a parent for posts/comments.
Create a post under which comments will be added for the member, including some later soft-deleted.
Generate comments for the specific member, including at least one normal and one to be soft-deleted by update.
Soft-delete a member's comment so the filter for is_deleted can yield results.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator advanced search and filtering for comments based on text (content) keywords. Ensure search returns only comments with matching keywords. Verify results honor soft-deleted visibility for the moderator role. Paginated results must be thoroughly checked.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a test member to create comments containing specific keywords.
Provide a topic for comment context.
Create a thread for post/comment assignment.
Produce a post attached to the thread, allowing comments to be tied to specific text.
Add several comments with varying content for use in search.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator's ability to filter and paginate comments based on deletion status (is_deleted) and created/updated date ranges. Confirm only proper comments are returned, and ensure both deleted and non-deleted comments can be discovered, including edge cases with no matches.

dependencies.purpose: Add test member for controlled comment creation.
Establish a context topic.
Thread for managing posts/comments.
Generate post where comments can be tested.
Insert comments for the test, some to be marked deleted.
Soft-delete one comment to enable is_deleted filter evaluation.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that an admin can fetch full details for a single comment using its unique id. Validate that the correct comment is returned with all schema-defined fields, including is_deleted status, content, member reference, post reference, and timestamps. Confirm that sensitive or privileged information is appropriately masked and correct error returned for invalid UUID.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member to author the comment to be fetched by id.
Insert a topic for contextual placement.
Provide a thread to attach posts/comments.
Post to which the comment will belong.
Create the comment and obtain its commentId for testing fetch by valid id.

scenarios.draft: Confirm that attempting to fetch a comment with an invalid, non-existent, or improperly formatted id returns a user-friendly not found or validation error. This covers edge case error handling for comment lookup.

Test successful thread creation as an admin under an existing, open topic. First, ensure an admin member exists and logs in, then as admin create a new topic using the respective endpoint (make sure the topic is open for new threads). After that, call this endpoint to create a new thread with a unique title. Verify the response includes all required thread fields and is associated with the correct topic and creator. Confirm the thread appears in the topic's thread list.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member who can act as the creator for topics/threads.
Create a new topic as an admin for use as the parent for thread creation.

scenarios.draft: Test thread creation in a topic that is closed to new threads. First, as admin, create a topic, then update the topic to set its closed flag to true. Then attempt to create a thread under the closed topic and verify the operation fails with a business rule violation (cannot create thread in closed topic).

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member to act as creator/context for the topic and thread.
Create a new topic.
Set the topic's closed flag to true (updating the topic to be closed before thread creation attempt).

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a thread with a duplicate title within a topic. First, create a topic, then create a thread with a specific title. Attempt to create another thread with the same title under the same topic and confirm that the business logic enforces unique thread titles within a topic, returning a duplicate error.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member to be the acting user and thread creator.
Create a new topic as the parent.
Create the initial thread with a specific title to establish the duplicate condition.

scenarios.draft: Test error response when trying to create a thread under a non-existent topic. Attempt to call the endpoint with a random or deleted topicId and confirm that the API returns a 404 not found or equivalent error message.

dependencies.purpose: Provision an admin user for authorization, even if the topic does not exist.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of a thread's title by the original thread creator (member). First, register a member, create a topic, then have the member create a thread. Next, as the thread owner, call the update endpoint to set a new unique title. Confirm the response reflects the updated thread, the changes are persisted, and audit logs (if available) attribute the update to the correct user.

dependencies.purpose: Register or create the member user who will be the thread creator.
Create the parent topic for thread creation.
Member creates the initial thread to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test business rule validation that prevents updating a thread's title to a duplicate of another thread within the same topic. Create a topic, add two threads with unique titles, then attempt to update the second thread's title to match the first. Confirm the API rejects the update and returns a duplicate error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user who can create and attempt to update threads.
Create the topic for thread operations.
Create both threads with unique titles for duplication test.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an unauthorized member (not the thread creator) cannot update another member's thread. Create two member users, a topic, have one member create a thread, and attempt to update the thread as the other member. Confirm that the API denies the update due to lack of ownership or permission.

dependencies.purpose: Register Member A (thread creator).
Register Member B (unauthorized updater).
Create the topic for the threads.
Have Member A create the thread.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can update any thread within a topic, regardless of original thread ownership. Register a moderator, create a topic, let a member create a thread, then as the moderator update the thread's title. Verify the changes are applied and audit trails are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create or register a moderator user.
Register a member to create the thread.
Establish the parent topic for the thread.
Have the member create the thread to be updated by the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator cannot update a thread with an invalid or empty title (business validation). Attempt to update as moderator with a blank or too-long title, and confirm the API returns input validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator user.
Register a member as thread creator.
Create the topic for thread operations.
Member creates the thread.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can update any thread's core fields within any topic. Register an admin, member, and topic; have the member create a thread, then as admin, update the thread. Confirm the thread's fields are updated and changes are reflected in subsequent fetches.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user.
Register a member who will create the thread.
Create the target topic.
Member creates thread to be updated by admin.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when the admin attempts to update a non-existent thread. Attempt the update with random or deleted threadId and verify the endpoint returns a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to perform the update.
Create a topic context if required for errors.

scenarios.draft: Test successful deletion of a thread by a moderator. Set up moderator, member, and topic, have the member create a thread, then as moderator delete the thread. Confirm the thread is no longer available in the topic's thread list and all cascading deletes are effective.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator user.
Register member (thread creator).
Create the topic where the thread is created.
Member creates thread for moderator to delete.

scenarios.draft: Test that a regular member cannot delete a thread via the moderator endpoint (unauthorized access). Register member, moderator, and topic; have member create a thread; then attempt to delete as the unauthorized member and confirm that access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for thread creation.
Register a moderator for authorization comparison.
Create a topic.
Member creates a thread to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A moderator creates a new flag on a specific post indicating a potential violation of community guidelines. The moderator selects a valid post ID, specifies the flag type (e.g., spam or abuse), provides a source (manual), and adds an optional note. The API should create the content flag and return the full flag record for tracking. Prerequisite: The target post must exist, and the acting user should have moderator privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid post as the flag target. The post must exist and be accessible to the moderator account before flagging.
Assign moderator role to a user, ensuring authorization to perform flag creation.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A moderator attempts to create a content flag with the same type on the same post more than once, triggering a uniqueness constraint. The first flag creation completes successfully. On the duplicate creation attempt (same post, type, and source), the API should reject the request, returning a meaningful error about duplicate flag constraints. This ensures that multiple identical flags for the same issue are not allowed. Prerequisites: Post exists and a moderator is authenticated.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post to be flagged. Required for associating flags to the specific post.
Assign moderator privileges to the test user.
Create the first content flag to establish the duplicate condition for the follow-up request.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A moderator attempts to create a content flag using a post_id or comment_id that does not exist in the system. The API should reject the request, responding with an error indicating that the target entity was not found, and no flag is created. This validates referential integrity and error reporting for invalid flag targets.

dependencies.purpose: Assign moderator role so user can attempt flag creation with arbitrary non-existent post/comment ID.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: An admin creates a new moderation flag on a comment to mark it for review. The admin specifies a valid comment_id, selects the appropriate flag type (e.g., inappropriate), and submits the request. On success, the API creates the new flag and returns the full record for referencing in future moderation actions. Prerequisites: The comment must exist, and the user must have admin authorization.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid comment to serve as the flag target.
Grant admin privileges to a user for authorization to perform the flag operation.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A user without moderator or admin privileges attempts to create a content flag via the admin endpoint. The API must reject this request, returning an authorization error confirming that only privileged roles can create content flags. The system audit log should capture this failed permission check. Prerequisites: Test user exists but does NOT have moderator or admin privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment to attempt flagging as an unauthorized user.
Register a member user to attempt the unauthorized action.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A moderator reviews an active content flag on a post and updates its status to cleared, indicating resolution. The moderator is authenticated, provides the update (such as cleared=true or status="resolved" in the payload), and the API returns the updated flag record reflecting the changes. This scenario verifies that flag lifecycle state transitions are functioning and auditable. Prerequisites: The flagged post exists, and the moderator has access.

dependencies.purpose: Create and persist a post to serve as the flag target.
Assign moderator rights so the update is authorized.
Create a content flag on the target post to set up a modifiable flag context.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: Moderator attempts to update an existing content flag but provides an invalid update, such as an unrecognized flag type or missing required field. The API should reject the request and return a validation or business logic error based on the schema. This ensures only valid updates are accepted and error handling is clear. Prerequisites: Need an existing flag and authenticated moderator; the payload is deliberately incorrect.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as the flag target.
Authorize user as moderator for update access.
Create an initial content flag to update in the negative test scenario.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: An admin updates an existing content flag to amend the type, add resolution notes, or clear the flag after reviewing. The admin provides a valid update payload and receives a full updated flag record on success. All changes are audit-logged. Prerequisites: Create a target comment, then flag it, and ensure the user is an admin.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a comment to be flagged.
Create/administer an admin account for authorization.
Create a content flag as setup for the update test.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A user who is not an admin attempts to update a content flag, for example to clear or modify its status/type. The API must deny the request due to insufficient privileges and return an appropriate authorization error. Prerequisites: A flag is created, and an ordinary member (not admin) attempts a flag update.

dependencies.purpose: Have a comment available for flagging and testing.
Create the flag as update target.
Create a regular member account for the unauthorized update attempt.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A moderator deletes (hard deletes) a content flag after resolving the issue or upon review. The API must remove the flag record from the database, and no subsequent retrieval should be possible. Audit logs should reflect the deletion. Prerequisites: Moderator privilege and an existing flag for deletion; deletion is irreversible.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a post exists to be flagged.
Grant moderator role for authorization.
Create a flag on the post to serve as the deletion candidate.

scenarios.draft: Scenario: A user lacking moderator or admin privileges attempts to delete a content flag. The API must deny the request, returning an appropriate authorization error, and the flag must remain in the system unchanged. Prerequisites: Prepare a flag, and ensure deletion is attempted by a non-privileged member user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to associate with the flag.
Create a flag to be the deletion target.
Create a normal member user for the unauthorized deletion attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully update a specific version of a comment. Precondition: an existing comment with multiple versions, where at least one version exists. The moderator attempts to change the content snapshot for one particular version. The expected outcome is that the update is committed and reflected in version history, with updated audit fields. Dependencies: comment and version creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as a member to serve as the target for versioning and moderation.
Add a version to the comment so that an existing version can be updated by the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that the moderator receives an error when attempting to update a comment version using a non-existent commentId or versionId. The scenario involves providing invalid UUIDs for either the comment or version. The expected response is a clear error message indicating not found. Dependencies: none needed for invalid ID test, but detail about error handling is verified.

Test that attempting to update a comment version as a user without moderator/admin privileges is forbidden. The scenario begins with a member creating a comment and version, followed by a non-privileged actor trying to update a version. The operation should fail and return an authorization error. Dependencies: comment creation, version creation, and simulation of session context as a non-privileged user.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment and version as a member for update attempt.
Create a version for the comment to attempt to update as a non-moderator.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can update a comment version's content snapshot. Precondition: there are comments with multiple versions. The admin user sends updated content for one version. Success is indicated by the persistence of the changes and updated audit fields. Dependencies: comment and version creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment for which a version will be added.
Create a version to be updated by the admin.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to update a comment version with invalid commentId or versionId as an admin. The scenario checks that the system returns appropriate not found errors for incorrect references.

Ensure that a user without admin or moderator privileges (e.g., a member) cannot use the admin endpoint to update a comment version. The test expects an authorization failure response. Preconditions: create a comment and version; attempt update as unauthorized user.

dependencies.purpose: Create the base comment for versioning.
Add a version to attempt update as a non-admin user.

scenarios.draft: Simulate an admin hard-deleting a specific comment version. Precondition: a comment with multiple versions exists. The designated version is deleted. The system should remove the version entry from history, maintain audit logs, and update UI views accordingly. Dependencies include comment and version creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment and add at least two versions so one can be deleted.
Add a version to the comment for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that deleting a version using an invalid commentId or versionId returns a not found error, ensuring the system properly handles references to non-existent records.

Verify that only admins can delete comment versions using the admin endpoint. A non-admin user attempts this operation and receives an authorization error. Precondition: a comment and at least one version exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create the base comment for the version.
Add a version to attempt unauthorized deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member who owns a comment can retrieve a list of all attachments associated with their comment. Comment must exist and have at least one attachment. Dependencies: comment creation, attachment creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member-owned comment for attachment.
Add at least one attachment to the comment.

scenarios.draft: Test the case where a member tries to list attachments for a commentId that does not exist. The expected outcome is a clear not found error response.

Test that a member who does not own the comment cannot list attachments for another user's comment if privacy restrictions apply. Preconditions: create a comment as member A, attempt to list attachments as member B (not owner nor moderator/admin). Expect a permission denied or filtered result. Dependencies: comment creation and session setup for different users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment as member A for ownership test.
Add an attachment to the comment owned by member A.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a moderator can retrieve all attachments for a specific comment, including those on comments owned by other users. The comment and at least one attachment must exist. The test confirms access and response accuracy. Dependencies: comment and attachment creation endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment with attachments for the moderator to retrieve.
Add one or more attachments to the comment for viewing.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to access attachments using a non-existent commentId as a moderator. Confirm that a not found error is returned and no data is leaked.

Ensure that a moderator can view attachments for any comment, even if the comment is private or restricted to the original owner. This verifies elevated privileges of moderators. The scenario includes comment and attachment creation and moderator access.

dependencies.purpose: Create a comment whose attachments are restricted for members but should be visible to moderators.
Add restricted attachment to the comment for moderator access validation.

scenarios.draft: Verify that a user (guest or authenticated) can successfully retrieve a paginated list of threads for an existing topic. The topic must exist and be active. The response should include summary details for all threads belonging to the specified topic, respecting pagination parameters. The test ensures only threads belonging to the specified topic are included and pagination works as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Fetch details of the topic to confirm it exists and extract its topicId for use in retrieving threads.
Create one or more threads in the topic as test data to ensure there are threads to return in the list.

scenarios.draft: Test that attempting to list threads for a non-existent topicId returns an appropriate not found error. The system should not return threads or an empty result, but an explicit error indicating the topic does not exist.

Validate that when a topic exists but has no threads, the endpoint returns an empty list in the paginated response. No error should occur; the response should be a paginated structure with zero entries.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm the existence of a topic and verify it is new or empty. Use this topic's topicId in the test.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for threads by partial or full title match within a topic. First, create a topic and several threads with varying titles (some containing the search term, others not). Submit a PATCH request with a search parameter for the title and verify the result only includes threads whose titles match the search. Verify pagination, sorting, and that irrelevant threads are excluded.

dependencies.purpose: Create test threads with specific titles to enable meaningful search filtering.

scenarios.draft: Verify that searching for threads within a topic using criteria that match no threads (e.g., non-existent keywords or creator) returns a paginated response with zero results, not an error.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a valid topic exists for the search operation.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to search threads using an invalid or non-existent topicId and verify that a clear error response is returned, rather than a silent empty result.

Test retrieving the full details for a specific thread under a topic. Create a new topic and a thread within it, then request the thread detail. Validate that the details match the data used to create the thread, and all relationships (topic, creator) are correctly reflected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread under a topic to ensure there is valid data for the lookup.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to retrieve a thread with a non-existent or invalid threadId under a valid topic. Confirm that the API returns an appropriate not found error and does not leak any internal state or unrelated information.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the topic exists and is valid to isolate the error condition to the threadId.

scenarios.draft: Try retrieving a thread using a valid threadId but with a topicId that does not match the thread's actual parent topic. The system should return an error, confirming referential integrity and ID relationship enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create a thread to obtain a valid threadId and its parent topicId for cross-check testing.
Set up a second topic with a different topicId for use as a mismatched parent in the test.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an authenticated member can create a thread under an existing, active topic. All required fields (title, topicId, creator info) must be present and valid. The test validates successful thread creation and ensures response data matches the request.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure a valid topic exists. Extract topicId for use in thread creation.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a thread in a topic that is closed (no longer accepting threads). The system should reject the request and return an error indicating that the topic is closed for new threads.

dependencies.purpose: Create or update a topic and mark it as closed, then attempt thread creation to validate business rule enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Check that trying to create two threads with the same title under the same topic fails on the second attempt, returning an error about title uniqueness per topic as enforced in the schema.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm topic exists.
Create an initial thread with a distinct title to prepare for a duplicate creation attempt.

scenarios.draft: Try to create a thread using a topicId that does not exist or is invalid, expecting an explicit error about the missing or invalid topic reference.

Ensure that a user with moderator privileges can successfully create a thread in an existing topic, following the same rules and validations as a regular member but with elevated permissions. Response should include the created thread's information.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm a valid, active topic exists to enable thread creation as a moderator.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a thread as a moderator in a topic marked as closed. The API should still enforce the closed status and return a business rule error, confirming that even privileged roles cannot override topic closure via this API.

dependencies.purpose: Create or update a topic and set its status to closed. Use this topicId to test that moderator creation is denied.

scenarios.draft: Check that a moderator attempting to create two threads with the same title under one topic receives a uniqueness error for the second creation, proving that title duplication is prevented across all roles.

dependencies.purpose: Confirm a topic exists for the test.
Create a first thread with a unique title before attempting duplicate creation as moderator.

scenarios.draft: Ensure that creating a thread as a moderator in a non-existent or invalid topic ID will result in a proper not found error, confirming referential and existence checks for thread creation.

Test retrieving the list of attachments for a post that has multiple attachments. First, create a member and an associated post. Then, upload multiple attachments to the post using the member's authentication. Finally, call the GET endpoint to verify that all uploaded attachments are correctly returned in the response, including their metadata (filename, mime type, upload time, etc.).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to attach files to. Requires valid member and thread context.
Upload one or more attachments to the created post to set up the test condition.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the list of attachments for a post that has no attachments. Start by creating a member and a post without uploading any attachments. Call the GET endpoint and verify that it returns an empty list, confirming no attachments are present for that post.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post without attachments. Valid member and thread setup needed.

scenarios.draft: Test searching attachments on a post by filename and MIME type. First, create a member, post, and upload several attachments with distinct filenames and types. Use the PATCH endpoint with search filters for a particular filename fragment and MIME type, and verify the returned list includes only matching attachments.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post to attach files to for test setup.
Upload multiple attachments with varied metadata to establish search test conditions.

scenarios.draft: Test searching for attachments using filters that do not match any attachments. Create a member, post, and upload some attachments. Then search using a rare or non-existent filename or MIME type and verify the response returns an empty list.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as context for attachments.
Add attachments to the post for negative search scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test failure case when submitting an invalid or malformed search query on attachments. Attempt to search with invalid data (e.g., unsupported filters, improperly formatted date ranges) and verify that the API returns a user-friendly error response indicating the nature of the problem.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for context. Attachment uploads may be optional here.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving metadata about a single attachment by its attachmentId and parent postId. Ensure the attachment exists by first creating a post and uploading an attachment. Confirm that the GET call returns accurate metadata including filename, file URI, uploader, MIME type, and timestamp.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post for attachment context.
Upload a new attachment and retrieve the ID for use in metadata retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to get details for an attachmentId that does not exist on a valid post. Create a post with valid member context but do not upload an attachment with the tested ID. Call the endpoint with a random or incorrect attachmentId and confirm a not found or error response is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent post.

scenarios.draft: Test successful upload and creation of an attachment on a post. Create a member, post, and then call this endpoint to upload a valid file attachment. Verify that the response contains accurate metadata including file URI, name, type, and that the attachment is linked to the correct post. Also ensure permissions are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post that will accept attachments.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when uploading an attachment with a file type or MIME type disallowed by business rules. Attempt to upload a file with an unsupported extension or MIME and confirm the operation fails with an error explaining the violation.

dependencies.purpose: Set up the post for attachment upload.

scenarios.draft: Test uploading an attachment as a user who is not permitted (e.g., not the post owner, or in a locked post). Attempt to upload an attachment as a different member or to a post in a locked state, and verify access is denied with an appropriate error message.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post context for a permission denial scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test updating file metadata (such as file name) for an attachment by the original member/uploader. Create a member, post, upload an attachment, and then use the PUT endpoint to modify allowed metadata. Confirm changes are reflected in the response and are stored.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post hosting the attachment.
Upload an attachment to provide an updatable target.

scenarios.draft: Test authorization failure when a user who did not upload the attachment attempts to update its metadata. Create an attachment with a member, then attempt update from a different member account. Confirm operation is denied and returns an appropriate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post context and first attachment as owner.
Create initial attachment as owner. Additional member can be created as needed.

scenarios.draft: Test error response when attempting to update metadata for an attachment that does not exist. Attempt to update using a random or invalid attachmentId (on a valid post), and validate an appropriate error is returned indicating the attachment cannot be found.

dependencies.purpose: Create the post for the update test context.

scenarios.draft: Test a successful update of a comment attachment's metadata (such as file name or URI) by the attachment's original uploader (member role). First, create a member and have them add a new comment under a post. Then, upload an attachment to this comment using the member account. Attempt to update modifiable metadata fields of this attachment, such as the attachment name or the download URI. Verify the operation succeeds and the updated metadata is returned. The scenario should validate that only fields allowed by business rules are changed, and that immutable properties (like upload timestamp) remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account who will own the comment and attachment.
Add a new comment as the member to associate the attachment with.
Upload an attachment to the comment as the member before attempting update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member who did not upload the attachment cannot update its metadata. First, create two different member accounts (member A and member B). Member A creates a comment and uploads an attachment. Member B attempts to update the metadata of member A's attachment. Verify the update is rejected with a permission-denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Create both member A (owner) and member B (non-owner).
Member A adds a new comment to associate the attachment.
Member A uploads an attachment to the comment before update attempt by member B.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can update the metadata of any comment attachment, even if not the original uploader. Create a member who uploads an attachment to their comment. Then, as a moderator, attempt to update the attachment's metadata (such as file name or URI). Confirm the operation is successful and proper audit/logs are created if required.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account who owns the comment and attachment.
Create a moderator account authorized to edit any attachment.
Have the member create a comment under which to upload the attachment.
Member uploads an attachment for later update by moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator cannot update immutable fields of an attachment (such as upload timestamp or foreign keys). Attempt an update where the request tries to modify an immutable field. Confirm that the operation fails with a validation error describing the forbidden update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account and have them upload an attachment to their comment.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can update the metadata of any comment attachment. First, create a member who uploads an attachment to a comment. dependencies.purpose: Register a member to upload the initial attachment.

Member uploads an attachment for later update by admin.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin attempting to update a non-existent attachment receives a not-found error. Attempt to update an attachment using invalid or missing IDs, and verify the error response is appropriate and descriptive.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user to perform the attempted update.

scenarios.draft: Test that the member who uploaded a comment attachment can delete it successfully. First, create a member, have them create a comment, and upload an attachment. scenarios.draft: Test that a different member (not the uploader) cannot delete an attachment uploaded by another member. Set up two members; member A uploads the attachment, member B tries to delete it, and confirm the system denies the deletion with an appropriate permission or authentication error.

dependencies.purpose: Register both member A (owner) and member B (non-owner).
Member A creates a comment and uploads an attachment.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator receives a not-found error when deleting a non-existent attachment. Attempt to delete an attachment using an invalid or unknown attachmentId, and confirm the system returns a not-found or appropriate error without affecting other records.

scenarios.draft: Test deletion of a comment attachment by an admin with valid permissions. First, create a board member and ensure the member is authenticated. As an admin, attempt to delete the uploaded attachment, and verify that the attachment is removed from the database and is no longer retrievable from the comment's attachment list. Audit logs should record the deletion event for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member to perform comment and attachment operations.

Upload an attachment to the created comment, establishing the necessary state for attachment deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test the admin's attempt to delete a comment attachment that does not exist. Attempt to delete an attachment using invalid or randomly generated IDs for both comment and attachment. The operation should fail and return a not found or error response, clearly indicating that the target attachment does not exist.

Test scenario where the admin attempts to delete a comment attachment without sufficient permissions (for example, the attachment is already deleted or the admin is not granted the needed privileges due to a privilege revocation event). The expected result is a permission denied error or appropriate error message, and the attachment remains in the system if it exists. Audit logs should document the failed deletion attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board member for ownership and scenario setup.
Add a comment by the created member.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated list of content reports by a moderator. First, create at least one member and one report by that member. Ensure the pagination works correctly and that the response structure aligns with the API contract.

scenarios.draft: Test the scenario where the moderator requests the list of reports, but none exist in the system. Expect an empty list or appropriate default structure, with no errors. Pagination metadata should be correct for an empty result set.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the report list as an admin when there are multiple reports in the system. dependencies.purpose: Create multiple members for reporting actions.
File separate reports as different members.

scenarios.draft: Test admin retrieval of the reports list when the system contains no reports. The response should be an empty list with valid pagination metadata, indicating no records present.

Test that users without admin privileges (such as members or guests) cannot access the admin report list endpoint. Attempt access as a non-admin and validate that the response is a forbidden error with no data leakage.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can perform complex queries over reports using filters such as status, content type, reporter, and date range. Prepare the system with several reports featuring different statuses and content, then perform filtered searches to ensure results only include matching records and are paginated correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Create members to generate diverse reports for search scenarios.
File multiple reports under different conditions (e.g., varying content type, status, reporter, and date).

scenarios.draft: Test the report search functionality when filters are applied that yield no matching results. The system should return an empty list and correct pagination information without error.

Attempt to access the advanced reports search as a user without moderator privileges (e.g., a regular member or guest). Verify the API refuses the request with a forbidden error and does not expose any report data.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can successfully apply different search filters over reports, such as by reporter, status, type, and time window. Set up the system with different report data, and validate that search results only return matching records, structured for pagination and summary display.

File several reports as those members for advanced search coverage.

scenarios.draft: Test the admin's ability to search reports using filters that currently yield no matches. The returned response should be an empty list and valid paging metadata, with no error raised.

Business rules: the version should be appended correctly, versionNumber is incremented, editor_member_id matches the requester, and the response includes the latest version data. event.scenario: Test that an admin can update the last_seen timestamp on an existing guest session, simulating an analytics update or ongoing visit. Verify that only updateable fields can be changed, and immutable fields remain untouched. Required business context: Admin privilege, guest session must exist.
event.review:
The draft test function takes a methodical approach to verifying that an admin can update a guest session's last_seen_at timestamp while ensuring other fields remain immutable:

- The initial guest session is created with random but valid values for all required properties.
- The update operation uses a genuinely new random value for last_seen_at and verifies that only this field is changed in the returned object.
- The test asserts that session_identifier, id, and first_seen_at remain unchanged after the update, validating immutability.
- Additionally, an attempt to update the id field is included to confirm that such updates are either ignored or ineffectual. Because id is not allowed in the update DTO and TypeScript will catch this, a type override or casting is (wrongly) used for the call; in reality, this should be omitted per the strict rules (id is not in IDiscussionBoardGuest.IUpdate, so the update body must never include extra properties).
- No authentication steps are included, in line with the API documentation assumption that the administrative context is implicit via connection.

**Corrections/Improvements:**
- The last test step (updating id via the update DTO) includes an illegal property and is against best practice and schema-based restrictions. This step should be omitted because the API schema will reject unknown properties (id is not allowed by DTO). Instead, focus assertions on confirming allowed fields update while others do not change.
- Make sure the random new timestamp differs not only from the original but, if repeatedly generated, could account for collision (while loop is sufficient for test purposes).
- Doc comments and variable naming are clear.

**Final recommendations:**

event.review:
전반적으로 테스트 시나리오의 요구 사항(활성/비활성 상태별, 시작/종료 시간 윈도우, 제목/본문 별 텍스트 매칭, 빈 검색 결과)에 맞게 설계를 완성해야 하며, 아래 세부 검증 항목이 반드시 만족되어야 한다.

- 생성 단계에서 실제로 다양한 조합의 system notice를 만들어야 필터의 의미가 있다. 적어도 아래 조건들을 망라하도록 케이스를 분기해야 한다.
  1) is_active: true, start_at=null, end_at=null   (상시 활성)
  2) is_active: true, start_at=과거, end_at=미래   (특정 기간 노출)
  3) is_active: false, start_at=과거, end_at=미래  (기간 중 비활성)
  4) is_active: true, start_at=미래, end_at=null   (미래 예정, 아직 노출 안 됨)
  5) 특이한 title/body 텍스트 (검색 테스트용)
- search 수행 시 각 조건이 정확히 반영되는지 확인
  - is_active true만 필터링 시, true인 공지만 포함되는지
  - is_active false만 필터링시, false인 공지만 포함되는지
  - 기간 필터(start_at_from, start_at_to, end_at_from, end_at_to) 검색: 타임라인 평면적으로 경계선과 겹치는 케이스 테스트
  - title, body 부분 일치 검색: 각기 다른 문자열을 포괄/배제하도록 설계
  - 빈 결과: 존재하지 않는 텍스트, 미래/과거만 반환하는 기간 등
- 반환된 목록(`data`)에 대해 각 created notice들의 id/title 등과 매칭시 실제 필터 조건 충족 여부를 체크해야 함
- 페이징 정보(pagination.current, limit, records, pages)에 대해서도 기본적인 합리성이 필요(특정 페이지, 개수, 총합 등)
- random/time 관련 입력 생성 시, 겹치지 않게 유니크 문자열/시간대를 분산하여 생성(예: 공지 제목에 고유 suffix 추가, start_at/end_at 충분히 벌리기)
- 단순 type assertion(typia.assert) 외에, TestValidator.predicate/equals 사용하여 실질적 비즈니스 조건을 검증할 것
- 테스트 메인 함수 내에 helper 함수를 정의할 수 있음(외부 import 없이 내부에서만 사용할 것)

- 주요 검증 요소는 1) 다양한 상태 데이터의 전체 노출(즉, 비활성/예약/만료/활성 모두 반환), 2) pagination 데이터 구조(모든 필드 존재), 3) 반환 데이터의 메타정보 필드 완비 등이다.
- 순서: (1) 다양한 상태의 시스템 공지사항 admin으로 등록 → (2) 모더레이터로 전체 목록 조회 → (3) pagination 필드 검증, (4) 생성한 ID 모두 존재 및 반환 배열 구조검증, (5) 데이터 메타 항목 존재 여부 검증
- 정상/에러(누락) 등 다양한 케이스는 데이터별로 반복 검증하고, 실제 생성→조회→필드점검 sequencing이 요구됨.

코드 품질 점검
- 타입 명확성 및 타입 체크(assert) 단계 모두 포함됨
- 입력값/응답객체 모두 DTO에 맞춰 있음
- 페이징 정보 및 notice 메타 필드 체크(predicate와 forEach)
- 중복/누락 데이터 방지용 ID matching 체크

수정/보완점 없음 (리뷰에서 모든 요구충족 및 누락 필드 없음)

최종 코드에서는 한글 상세 주석 및 명확한 순번 설명이 포함되어 가독성, 유지보수성 모두 우수함.

event.think_again_with_compile_error: The error `Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'HeaderValue'` is caused by attempting to explicitly assign undefined to the Authorization field in headers when constructing the nonAdminConnection. The IConnection.headers type does not allow undefined for header values—removing the field entirely is the way to simulate a request without the Authorization header. Instead of setting `Authorization: undefined`, simply omit the Authorization property from the headers object (i.e., remove it instead of assigning undefined). The fix is to destructure the original headers, then spread all fields except Authorization, constructing a new object without that property.
